<!-- source: guide/setup.md -->

# Set up a project

`awa setup` connects a project folder to a model. It writes the model provider and its key into
the project's `.env` file, and optionally a database and tracing. It writes nowhere else and never
prints a value.

In a terminal, run it without options. It asks section by section; then `awa doctor` checks the
result:

```console
awa setup
awa doctor
```

The page **Set up** of the web app does the same for the model ([The web app](web-app.md#set-up)).

## In a script

In a script, pass the answers as options. A key is read from standard input, never as a
command-line value:

```console
awa setup --provider openai --key-stdin < key.txt
awa setup --database postgres-docker --yes
```

Without a terminal and without options, `awa setup` changes nothing. It prints the state of every
section and the options to use.

## The sections

| Section | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| provider | Saves the key of one provider: `anthropic`, `openai`, `azure_openai` (key, endpoint and deployment), `google_genai`, `mistralai`, `groq`, or `ollama` (where it listens). The key is typed hidden or read with `--key-stdin`. |
| test | `--test` makes one tiny call (one output token, 15 seconds at most) to the `default` model and records whether it answered. |
| database | `sqlite` (the default): local files next to the blueprint. `postgres-docker`: PostgreSQL in Docker on this computer, with a generated password. `url`: your own PostgreSQL, read with `--database-url-stdin` and tested with `SELECT 1` before it is saved. |
| tracing | `off`, `langfuse-docker` (Langfuse in Docker with its first user and project keys generated; Docker needs at least 4 GB of memory), or `url` (your own Langfuse: `--langfuse-url`, `--langfuse-public-key`, and the secret key with `--langfuse-secret-stdin`). |

Most projects need only the provider. The defaults for the database (local files) and tracing
(off) work without setup.

### Which model is used

You usually do not set a model. When `AWA_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `AWA_FAST_MODEL` and `AWA_STRONG_MODEL`
are not set, awa takes them from the provider whose credentials are complete, in this order:
Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google, Mistral, Groq, Ollama.

- With only Azure OpenAI set up, every profile uses your deployment, and nothing asks for
  another key.
- When you choose a provider that is not first in that order, `awa setup` also writes the three
  model settings ([Models](../develop/models.md)).

### Changing a value

- A value already in `.env` is changed only after you confirm it: answer the question in a
  terminal, or pass `--yes`.
- Before it writes, `awa setup` keeps one copy of the old file as `.env.bak`. Like `.env`, only
  you can read it.
- Without a terminal and without `--yes`, it stops with exit code 3 and names the settings.

## Local services

PostgreSQL and Langfuse can run in Docker on this computer, one set per project:

```console
awa setup services up --profile db
awa setup services status
awa setup services down
awa setup services down --volumes --confirm awa-my-desk-1a2b3c4d
```

- Each project gets its own Compose project name, `awa-<folder>-<8 characters of a hash of its
  path>`. Two projects never share or delete each other's containers or data.
- Every port is bound to `127.0.0.1`, so nothing is reachable from other computers. A taken port
  is skipped for the next free one.
- The Compose file is `.awa/compose.services.yaml` and holds no password. The generated passwords
  are kept in `.env` only (`AWA_SETUP_*`).
- `down` keeps the data. `down --volumes` deletes it and needs the project name typed, or
  `--confirm`.
- Without Docker, `awa setup` says so in one sentence. Use `--database url` or `--tracing url`
  with a server you have.

## See and change single settings

- `awa env list` shows every setting: its value (secrets only as `set` or `not set`), where it
  comes from (`env`, `.env:<line>` or `default`) and what uses it.
- `awa env set NAME` changes one setting in `.env`. A secret is typed hidden or read with
  `--stdin`.

Every setting is in the [Settings reference](../reference/settings.md).

## Common mistakes

| You see | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `credentials ABSENT` in `awa doctor` | The key is not in the `.env` of the folder you run awa in; run `awa setup` there. |
| Exit code 3 | A value would be replaced without a terminal: add `--yes`, or run it in a terminal. |
| Langfuse in Docker does not start | Give Docker at least 4 GB of memory. |

<!-- guide:do cd . -->

!!! example "In code"

    `awa.setup()` is the same in a notebook or a script: without arguments it reports the state of every section and
    changes nothing; what you pass, such as `awa.setup(provider="openai", api_key=key)`, is written to `.env`.

    <!-- guide:python -->
    ```python
    import awa

    plan = awa.setup()
    for section in plan.status():
        print(section.section, section.state, section.detail)
    ```

    Before a key is set, it prints:

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    provider missing no model key is set
    test missing set a key first
    database set local files next to the blueprint (SQLite and JSON)
    tracing set off
    ```

<!-- source: guide/describe.md -->

# Describe a process

Tell awa in a few sentences what your process does, and awa drafts the system for you. The draft is a
[**blueprint**](../reference/glossary.md#blueprint): the file `blueprint.yaml` with the agents, their tools, how they
work together and which steps wait for a person. You read it, adapt it and test it before you rely on it.

The shortest path is one command:

```console
awa build "Supplier invoices arrive by email as PDF files. Accounts payable checks each one against the purchase order in our ERP. The vendor must match and the amount may differ by at most 1 percent. Above 10,000 EUR the head of finance approves the payment. A mismatch goes on hold, and the supplier is told why." --out my-process
```

There are three ways to a blueprint. All three end in the same file: `awa validate` checks it, `awa show` explains
it and `awa eval` tests it.

| Way | You give | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [In your own words](#in-your-own-words) | A few sentences | You know the process but not the agents. This is the recommended way. |
| [From a template](#from-a-template) | A template name | You want a small working project to change. |
| [By hand](#by-hand) | A YAML file | You know what you want, or you change a project awa made. |

<!-- guide:do cd . -->

!!! info "Preview"
    Letting awa write the blueprint (`awa build`, the page **Describe**) works and is tested, but its options may still change in a minor release ([Stability](../about/stability.md)).

## In your own words

Use the page **Describe** of the web app, or `awa build` in a terminal. The
[guided tour](tour.md#step-4-describe-the-process) builds the invoice desk this way; the step numbers in the legend
are those of the tour.

![The Describe page: your files and your ledger from step 3, the description in the large box, the switch for automatic testing and the Create my system button](../assets/screenshots/guide/a04-describe-before.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a04-describe-before.legend.txt"

The same in a terminal, with the folder of your files:

```console
awa build "Supplier invoices arrive as PDF files. ..." --out invoice-desk --data invoice-files
```

### What a good description says

| Say ... | Example |
| --- | --- |
| What starts the process and what arrives | "Supplier invoices arrive as PDF files." |
| Each step and who does it today | "Accounts payable checks the invoice against the purchase order." |
| Every rule with its numbers | "The amount may differ by at most 1 percent." |
| Every decision a person makes, and from when | "From 5,000 EUR the head of finance approves." |
| The systems involved, by what they are | "our ERP", "the shared mailbox", "Jira" |
| What happens when something is wrong | "A mismatch goes on hold and the supplier is told why." |
| What comes out at the end | "The invoice is booked, or on hold with a reason." |

Describe the business, not how the AI should think. "Handle our invoices with AI" gives a system that guesses. The
description at the top of this page gives one that can be tested.

### What awa does with it

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    D["Your description<br/>and files"] --> T["Write the eval cases,<br/>rules and approvals"]
    T --> A["Design the agents"]
    A --> E["Run every case"]
    E -- "a case fails" --> R["Repair the design"]
    R --> E
    E -- "target reached or<br/>rounds used up" --> P["Write the project folder"]
```

1. **Tests first.** From your words awa writes the eval cases, the rules with their numbers, and the decisions that
   a person makes, each with its condition (for example `amount_eur >= 5000`). Where your text is silent, awa makes
   a choice and lists it under **Assumptions** in `README.md`. When your text says what starts the process ("every
   Monday", "when a file lands in a folder"), awa adds that trigger.
2. **Design against the tests.** awa designs the agents, their tools and how they work together. It checks the
   design and has it repaired before it goes on.
3. **Evaluate and repair.** Every case runs. A case that fails twice goes back with what happened, and awa changes
   the design while the tests stay fixed. This repeats until all cases pass, the rounds are used up (three by
   default) or the usage limit is reached.
4. **Write the project folder**, with `CONNECT.md` for every system that still works on a stand-in.

**Rules become code, not instructions.** "The amount may differ by at most 1 percent" becomes a small function in
`tools.py`, checked against a worked example. "From 5,000 EUR the head of finance approves" becomes an approval step
with a condition. Neither is left to the model's judgment.

The options of `awa build` you need most:

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--out DIR` | The project folder. Without it awa uses the name of the system. |
| `--data PATH`, `--note FILE=TEXT` | Your files and what must happen with them ([Your files](files.md#build-on-your-files)). |
| `--rounds N` | How often awa may test and repair the design (default 3). |
| `--target R` | The pass rate to stop at (default 1.0, every case). Below it the command ends with exit code 1. |
| `--force` | Replace an existing project folder. |

The others, such as `--guidance` for an extra design requirement or a cap on the model calls of the whole build,
are in the [command reference](../reference/cli.md#awa-build).

**When the result misses something:**

1. Read `README.md`: are the acceptance criteria and the assumptions right?
2. Read `evals/cases.yaml`: are the exceptions covered?
3. Run `awa show blueprint.yaml`: who does what, and which steps wait for a person?
4. Add what is missing to the description and build again with `--force`.

## From a template

A template is a small project that works at once. There are five:

- `minimal`: one agent with a lookup tool and an action that asks first.
- `team`: a lead with a researcher and a writer.
- `workflow`: fixed steps.
- `network`: teammates on a shared task board.
- `support`: a support desk with a refund approval.

<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ awa init support-desk --template support
created support-desk (template support):
  blueprint.yaml
  tools.py
  tests/conftest.py
  tests/test_blueprint.py
  evals/cases.yaml
  .env.example
  .gitignore
  README.md
  pyproject.toml

next:
  cd support-desk
  pip install pytest         if it is missing
  pytest                     offline tests, no key
  awa setup                  set your provider's key in .env (or: awa ui, then Set up)
  awa chat blueprint.yaml    tools.py next to the blueprint is loaded by itself
$ cd support-desk
$ awa validate blueprint.yaml
support-desk: valid
$ awa show blueprint.yaml
support-desk 0.1.0
Answers customer requests about orders, deliveries and refunds.
entrypoint: team

agent             model    tools                         skills               description
triage            default  -                             delegation-briefs    Receives every customer request, gets the facts and write...
order_specialist  default  lookup_order, track_shipment  -                    Looks up orders and shipments and reports their status.
refunds           default  lookup_order, issue_refund    safe-tool-execution  Handles refund requests end to end and talks to the custo...

team support-desk: orchestrator triage
  delegates: triage -> order_specialist, refunds
  handoffs: triage -> refunds
  handoffs: refunds -> triage
  shared: messaging

approvals: issue_refund
```

You can check a template without a key. It comes with offline tests (`pytest`) and eval cases for `awa eval`. Then
change the agents' instructions, rename the tools and add your own eval cases.

## By hand

<!-- guide:do cd . -->

### Let awa write the file

`awa new process` writes a blueprint from the agents and their tasks. Without options it asks one question at a
time. With options it runs without questions:

<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ awa new process refund-desk --agent triage="Answers order questions and passes refund requests on" --agent refunds="Checks a refund request and asks for approval before paying" --structure team --lead triage --no-input -o refund-desk.yaml
wrote refund-desk.yaml

auto-matching for refund_desk
  triage
    + skill orchestration-planning (role: orchestrator)
    + skill refund-and-credit-requests (matched: order, refund, requests)
  refunds
    + skill refund-and-credit-requests (matched: refunds, request, asks, approval)
    + skill approval-requests (matched: request, approval)

next:
  awa show refund-desk.yaml
  awa run refund-desk.yaml "<a task for the team>"
  awa add trigger refund-desk.yaml   # start it by itself: schedule, web request, ...
$ awa validate refund-desk.yaml
refund_desk: valid (tool names not checked; no tools.py beside it)
```

The lines with `+` are **skills** that awa added by itself. A skill is a written method that an agent follows. With
`auto: true` in a blueprint, awa matches skills and ready-made tools to each agent by the words of its task. It never
calls a model for this, so the same blueprint always gives the same result. A tool that sends, writes or deletes is
never added this way: awa only suggests it, and `awa validate` warns about it.

### Write it yourself

A blueprint is a YAML file: `name: value` lines, with two spaces of indentation for what belongs together. In this
example, one agent reads a table of orders and writes reminder emails, and a person approves every email:

<!-- guide:file reminder-desk/blueprint.yaml -->
```yaml
name: reminder-desk
description: Finds overdue orders and writes a reminder for each one.
defaults:
  model: default

toolkits:
  files: {root: ./data}
  email: {sender: accounting@example.com, allowed_recipients: ["@example.com"]}

agents:
  - name: reminder_writer
    description: Finds overdue orders and writes the reminders.
    instructions: Read orders.csv with read_csv. For each overdue order, send a short reminder with send_email.
    tools: [builtin:read_csv, builtin:send_email]

approvals:
  - tool: builtin:send_email
```

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `name`, `description` | What the system is called and what it does. Names use letters, digits, `_` and `-`. |
| `defaults` | Settings every agent shares, such as the model profile (`default`, `fast` or `strong`). |
| `toolkits` | Settings of ready-made tools. Here the file tools only see the folder `data`, and mail may only go to `@example.com`. |
| `agents` | Each agent with its job (`description`), its `instructions` and the `tools` it may use. |
| `approvals` | The tools that wait for a person before they run ([Approvals](approvals.md)). |

`awa validate` checks the file without a key and without a model. `awa show` explains it:

<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ awa validate reminder-desk/blueprint.yaml
reminder-desk: valid (tool names not checked; no tools.py beside it)
$ awa show reminder-desk/blueprint.yaml
reminder-desk 1.0.0
Finds overdue orders and writes a reminder for each one.
entrypoint: reminder_writer

agent            model    tools                 skills  description
reminder_writer  default  read_csv, send_email  -       Finds overdue orders and writes the reminders.

approvals: send_email
```

An entry of `tools` is one of these:

- `builtin:<tool>`: a tool that ships with awa.
- `connector:<system>` or `connector:<system>.<operation>`: a system you connected ([Connect systems](connect.md)).
- `mcp:<server>`: the tools of an MCP server.
- The plain name of a function in `tools.py` next to the blueprint.

How agents work together (`team`, `workflow`, `network`) is the subject of [Agents and teams](agents-and-teams.md).
Every key of the format is in [Blueprints](../develop/blueprints.md).

## Many conditions and special cases

A real process has tiers, exceptions and blocked suppliers. Keep every special case as **one row in a table, one rule
that decides it, and one test that checks it**:

| # | If ... | then ... | Decided by | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the invoice is below 5,000 EUR and open | release it | the rule | `small-invoice` |
| 2 | the amount is 5,000 EUR up to 20,000 EUR | ask the head of finance | the head of finance | `finance-tier` |
| 3 | the amount is 20,000 EUR or more | ask the management board | the board | `board-tier` |
| 4 | the invoice is already paid | never pay it again | the rule | `paid-invoice` |
| 5 | the supplier is on the blocked list | do not pay; say why | the rule | `blocked-supplier` |

Check the table before you build it:

- Gaps and overlaps: who decides exactly 20,000?
- A rule or a person for every row.
- What happens when a value is missing.

Then each kind of row goes to one place:

| The row is | It lives in |
| --- | --- |
| A number that decides whether a person must approve | An approval condition (`when`) |
| A calculation or lookup that must always give the same answer | A small rule in `tools.py` |
| A fixed order of steps | A workflow ([Agents and teams](agents-and-teams.md)) |
| Judgment that cannot be written as a rule | The agent's instructions, and an eval case |

### Write the rules

Work on a copy of the desk from the tour: copy the folder `invoice-desk` to `desk-rules`. Replace its `tools.py`
with two **rules** and two **approval steps**:

<!-- guide:do copy invoice-desk desk-rules -->
<!-- guide:do cd desk-rules -->
<!-- guide:file tools.py -->
```python
"""The rules and approval steps of the invoice desk, with three tiers and a blocked-supplier list."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

from awa import tool

BLOCKED_SUPPLIERS = {"Blocked Supplies Ltd"}

@tool
def payment_route(amount_eur: float) -> str:
    """Who must approve a payment: release (under 5,000 EUR), finance (from 5,000 EUR up to 20,000 EUR) or board (from 20,000 EUR).

    Args:
        amount_eur: The amount in EUR.
    """

    if amount_eur >= 20000:
        return "board"
    if amount_eur >= 5000:
        return "finance"
    return "release"

@tool
def supplier_status(supplier: str) -> str:
    """Whether a supplier may be paid: ok or blocked.

    Args:
        supplier: The name of the supplier as on the invoice.
    """

    return "blocked" if supplier in BLOCKED_SUPPLIERS else "ok"

@tool
def finance_approval(invoice_id: str, amount_eur: float) -> str:
    """The head of finance approves payments from 5,000 EUR up to 20,000 EUR.

    Args:
        invoice_id: The invoice number.
        amount_eur: The amount in EUR.
    """

    return json.dumps({"approved": True, "invoice_id": invoice_id, "amount_eur": amount_eur})

@tool
def board_approval(invoice_id: str, amount_eur: float) -> str:
    """The management board approves payments from 20,000 EUR.

    Args:
        invoice_id: The invoice number.
        amount_eur: The amount in EUR.
    """

    return json.dumps({"approved": True, "invoice_id": invoice_id, "amount_eur": amount_eur})

__all__ = ["board_approval", "finance_approval", "payment_route", "supplier_status"]
```

A **rule** gives the same answer for the same input. The agent decides when to call it, so an eval case checks the
call (`tool:payment_route`).

An **approval step** is a tool that a person must approve. Each tier is its own tool with its own condition, with no
gap and no overlap:

<!-- guide:file blueprint.yaml -->
```yaml
format_version: awa/v1
name: invoice_desk
description: Checks supplier invoices against the ledger and releases them for payment.
agents:
- name: invoice_checker
  description: Looks the invoice up in the ledger and checks its purchase order.
  instructions: Look the invoice up in the invoices table with invoice_ledger_query. Report the supplier, the purchase order, the amount in EUR and the status.
  tools:
  - connector:invoice_ledger.query
- name: payment_clerk
  description: Releases checked, open invoices for payment.
  instructions: |
    1. Call supplier_status with the supplier. A blocked supplier is never paid: say so and stop.
    2. Call payment_route with the amount. For release, confirm the release. For finance call finance_approval, for board call board_approval, then confirm the release.
    3. Never release an invoice that is already paid.
  tools:
  - supplier_status
  - payment_route
  - finance_approval
  - board_approval
entrypoint: workflow
workflow:
  sequential:
  - invoice_checker
  - payment_clerk
approvals:
- tool: finance_approval
  when: amount_eur >= 5000 and amount_eur < 20000
- tool: board_approval
  when: amount_eur >= 20000
connectors:
  invoice_ledger:
    use: sql
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: INVOICE_LEDGER_DATABASE_URL
    read_only: true
```

`awa tools call` runs one tool of `tools.py` without a model and without a key. It is the cheapest test of a rule.
The arguments come from small files, `big.json`:

<!-- guide:file big.json -->
```json
{"amount_eur": 25000}
```

and `small.json`:

<!-- guide:file small.json -->
```json
{"amount_eur": 4999.99}
```

<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ awa validate blueprint.yaml
invoice_desk: valid
$ awa show blueprint.yaml
invoice_desk 1.0.0
Checks supplier invoices against the ledger and releases them for payment.
entrypoint: workflow

agent            model    tools                                                             skills  description
invoice_checker  default  invoice_ledger_query                                              -       Looks the invoice up in the ledger and checks its purchas...
payment_clerk    default  supplier_status, payment_route, finance_approval, board_approval  -       Releases checked, open invoices for payment.

workflow: invoice_checker -> payment_clerk

approvals: finance_approval (when amount_eur >= 5000 and amount_eur < 20000), board_approval (when amount_eur >= 20000)
$ awa tools call tools.py payment_route --args "@big.json"
board
$ awa tools call tools.py payment_route --args "@small.json"
release
```

Files work the same in every terminal; Windows PowerShell 5.1 removes the double quotes inside an argument such as
`'{"amount_eur": 25000}'`.

### Test the boundaries

Try each condition with the values around each limit. This script uses the same condition object that awa uses:

<!-- guide:python -->
```python
from awa.tools import ApprovalCondition

finance = ApprovalCondition("amount_eur >= 5000 and amount_eur < 20000")
board = ApprovalCondition("amount_eur >= 20000")
for amount in (4999.99, 5000, 19999.99, 20000):
    print(f"{amount:>9}  finance asks: {finance({'amount_eur': amount})!s:5}  board asks: {board({'amount_eur': amount})}")
```

<!-- guide:expect -->
```text
  4999.99  finance asks: False  board asks: False
     5000  finance asks: True   board asks: False
 19999.99  finance asks: True   board asks: False
    20000  finance asks: False  board asks: True
```

From 5,000 up, exactly one of the two asks, never both. When a condition cannot be worked out, it **asks** rather than
guesses. That happens when the value is missing, or when it can be read two ways (`5.000` is five thousand or five):

<!-- guide:python -->
```python
from awa.tools import ApprovalCondition

finance = ApprovalCondition("amount_eur >= 5000 and amount_eur < 20000")
print("missing amount asks:", finance({}))
print("'5.000' asks:", finance({"amount_eur": "5.000"}))
print("'5,000' asks:", finance({"amount_eur": "5,000"}))
```

<!-- guide:expect -->
```text
missing amount asks: True
'5.000' asks: True
'5,000' asks: True
```

A tool with a required number refuses a call without it, before anything happens:

<!-- guide:run exit=1 -->
```console
$ awa tools call tools.py payment_route
error: missing arguments: amount_eur. The tool takes payment_route(amount_eur: number)
```

### What conditions cannot do

- **They see only the tool's own values.** A rule must compute a month's total or the person who asked, and pass it
  to the approval step as an input.
- **One approval per tool.** Tiers need one tool each, as above.
- **Nothing forces a rule to run before an action.** awa enforces the approval on the tool that acts, not the order
  that the instructions ask for. Put the safety there.
- **Branches without the model exist only in a `process:`, and only forward**
  ([below](#a-process-with-checked-steps)). In a `workflow:` the agent picks the branch by its instructions, so test
  every branch with one case per row.

### A rule table

You can also write the worksheet as a table and let awa find the boundaries:

- The first row that holds decides.
- `else` decides when no row holds.
- A missing or unclear value goes to `when_unclear`: a person decides, unless you say `reject`.

<!-- guide:python -->
```python
from awa.workflows import SpecialCases, boundary_cases

cases = SpecialCases.model_validate({
    "cases": [
        {"if": [{"field": "amount_eur", "op": ">=", "value": 5000}], "then": "ask", "by": "finance"},
        {"if": [{"field": "amount_eur", "op": "<", "value": 5000},
                {"field": "supplier", "op": "one of", "value": ["Acme Tools"]}],
         "then": "approve"},
    ],
    "else": "ask",
})
for line in cases.describe():
    print(line)
for case in boundary_cases(cases):
    if case.row == 2:
        print(f"{case.probe:<36} {case.expected.describe()}")
```

<!-- guide:expect -->
```text
If amount is 5,000 EUR or more: a person decides (finance)
If amount is less than 5,000 EUR and supplier is one of "Acme Tools": approved without asking a person
Otherwise: a person decides
When a value is missing or unclear: a person decides
amount_eur just below 5,000 EUR      row 2: approved without asking a person
amount_eur exactly 5,000 EUR         row 1: a person decides (finance)
amount_eur just above 5,000 EUR      row 1: a person decides (finance)
supplier not in the list             else: a person decides
supplier "Acme Tools" in other case  else: a person decides
amount_eur missing                   unclear at row 1 (amount_eur has no value): a person decides
amount_eur two-way number 5.000      unclear at row 1 (the number '5.000' in amount_eur can be read two ways (decimal or thousands)): a person decides
supplier missing                     unclear at row 2 (supplier has no value): a person decides
supplier two-way number 5.000        else: a person decides
```

Text must match exactly, including capital letters: "Acme Tools" in other case goes to `else`. In a blueprint, the
same table goes under `special_cases:`. `awa show cases blueprint.yaml` prints the rows and every boundary with its
outcome ([Blueprints: special cases](../develop/blueprints.md#special-cases)).

### A process with checked steps

A `process:` in a blueprint is a line of checked steps. A rule table named after a step decides on that step's
result in every run, and a step can be tried again when it fails.

The **dry run** walks such a process without a model. Stand-in agents answer with the values you give, and the dry
run prints the path a run would take:

<!-- guide:python -->
```python
import asyncio

from awa.blueprints import Blueprint, dry_run
from awa.persistence import StateInMemorySaver

blueprint = Blueprint.from_yaml_text("""
name: invoice-route
agents:
  - name: reader
    description: Reads one invoice.
    output_schema:
      type: object
      properties: {supplier: {type: string}, amount_eur: {type: number}}
      required: [supplier, amount_eur]
  - name: archivist
    description: Files the invoice.
process:
  - name: extract
    agent: reader
    retry: {max_attempts: 3, initial: 10s}
    after_last_try: ask
    checks:
      - {kind: rule, fail_when: "amount_eur <= 0", message: No amount found.}
  - name: archive
    agent: archivist
special_cases:
  extract:
    cases:
      - {if: "supplier in ['Blocked Supplies Ltd']", then: reject, message: Blocked supplier.}
      - {if: [{field: amount_eur, op: ">=", value: 5000}], then: ask, by: finance}
      - {if: [{field: amount_eur, op: "<", value: 5000}], then: approve}
    else: ask
""")
for values, fail in (
    ({"supplier": "Acme Tools", "amount_eur": 1200}, {"extract": 2}),
    ({"supplier": "Acme Tools", "amount_eur": 6200}, {}),
    ({"supplier": "Blocked Supplies Ltd", "amount_eur": 300}, {}),
):
    path = asyncio.run(dry_run(blueprint, values, checkpointer=StateInMemorySaver(), fail=fail))
    print(f"{values['amount_eur']} from {values['supplier']}: {path.outcome}")
    for line in path.lines:
        print(f"  {line.step}: {line.text}")
```

<!-- guide:expect -->
```text
1200 from Acme Tools: completed
  extract: Try 1 of 3 failed: ModelProviderError: simulated failure of try 1 (dry run). A real run waits 10 s, then tries again.
  extract: Try 2 of 3 failed: ModelProviderError: simulated failure of try 2 (dry run). A real run waits 20 s, then tries again.
  extract: passed its checks (try 3). Special case row 3 (If amount is less than 5,000 EUR: approved without asking a person).
  archive: passed its checks.
6200 from Acme Tools: completed
  extract: PAUSE: a person is asked: Special case: row 2: a person decides (finance). The dry run answers approve.
  extract: passed its checks (try 1). Special case row 2 (If amount is 5,000 EUR or more: a person decides (finance)).
  archive: passed its checks.
300 from Blocked Supplies Ltd: rejected
  extract: REJECTED by special case row 1 (If supplier is one of "Blocked Supplies Ltd": rejected. Blocked supplier.).
```

- The first invoice fails twice and passes on the third try. (`fail` makes the stand-in raise an error, as a
  provider outage would.)
- The second pauses for finance.
- The third is rejected, and the archive step never starts.

On the command line: `awa show dry-run blueprint.yaml --input values.json --fail extract=2`, with the values in a
JSON file. The dry run proves the routing only. It reads no documents, calls no tools and shows nothing a model would
answer.

## Common mistakes

| Mistake | What you see | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The description is one vague sentence | Many assumptions in `README.md` | Add what arrives, the rules with numbers and who decides. |
| A rule is left to the model | An eval case fails now and then | Give it a number; awa turns it into a rule or an approval. |
| The description is not in quotes in the terminal | `unrecognized arguments` | Put the whole text in double quotes, or use the page **Describe**. |
| One space or a tab as indentation in YAML | A parse error with a line number | Use two spaces per level, no tabs. |
| A tool name is misspelled | `awa validate` says the tool is unknown | Copy the name from `awa show`. |
| Two conditions overlap or leave a gap | Two approvals ask, or none | Use `>=` on one side and `<` on the other; test the boundary values. |

<!-- guide:do cd . -->

!!! example "In code"

    A blueprint is a Python object too. `Blueprint.from_yaml_file` reads and checks the file;
    `awa.blueprints.build_project` is `awa build` from Python ([Blueprints](../develop/blueprints.md)).

    <!-- guide:python -->
    ```python
    from awa.blueprints import Blueprint

    blueprint = Blueprint.from_yaml_file("reminder-desk/blueprint.yaml")
    print(blueprint.name, [agent.name for agent in blueprint.agents])
    print([approval.tool for approval in blueprint.approvals])
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    reminder-desk ['reminder_writer']
    ['builtin:send_email']
    ```

<!-- source: guide/files.md -->

# Your files

Use this page when your process works on files: invoices, orders, lists, emails. awa reads your files, builds the
process on what they really contain, tests it on copies, and then runs it on each file. Your originals are never
changed.

Three commands get you from a folder of files to results:

```console
awa data inspect invoices/
awa build "<your process>" --out my-desk --data invoices/
awa data run my-desk --all
```

1. `awa data inspect` shows what is in the files.
2. `awa build` designs and tests the process on them.
3. `awa data run` runs the process once for each file.

The sections below walk through each step. Some of them use a finished example from the awa folder,
`examples/benchmarks/core/04_document_intake`: an invoice inbox with a PDF, a Word file, an Excel file and a scan.
Copy it to your work folder as `intake-desk`:

<!-- guide:do cd . -->
<!-- guide:do copy awa:examples/benchmarks/core/04_document_intake intake-desk -->
<!-- guide:do cd intake-desk -->

!!! info "Preview"
    `awa data` and building on your files work and are tested, but their options may still change in a minor release ([Stability](../about/stability.md)).

## See what awa finds

Start here. awa reads every file without a model, says what is in it, and flags what is unusual. Nothing is changed.

- In the web app, open the page **Data**: one card per file, as in
  [step 3 of the tour](tour.md#step-3-bring-your-files-and-your-ledger).
- In a terminal, run `awa data inspect` with files, folders or patterns:

<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ awa data inspect data
6 files, 3 tables, 20 rows, 6 warnings, 0 errors

file                         kind  content                status  flags
inbox/2024-0412_mueller.pdf  pdf   1 page (born digital)  ok      -
inbox/88231_zuercher.docx    docx  7 paragraphs           ok      -
inbox/ln-2024-17_meyer.xlsx  xlsx  16 rows                ok      3 warnings
inbox/scan_0001.pdf          pdf   1 page (scanned)       ok      1 warning
purchase_orders.json         json  -                      ok      -
vendors.csv                  csv   4 rows                 ok      2 warnings
...
  [warning] 1 of 1 analyzed pages have no usable text layer; they need OCR
...
```

A warning is something to know, not a failure. `--verbose` also prints the code of each flag. The flags in this
example:

| Flag | In file | What it means for you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DF-W-NO-TEXT-LAYER` | `scan_0001.pdf` | The page is a picture without a text layer. The `workspace` connector reads it with a vision model, one model call per page; without that, hold it for manual entry. |
| `DF-W-TOTALS-ROW` | `ln-2024-17_meyer.xlsx` | Rows 10 to 12 are totals and are not counted as data. |
| `DF-W-NO-HEADER` | `ln-2024-17_meyer.xlsx` | The sheet `Kopf` has no row with column names; the columns are named A, B, and so on. |
| `DF-W-ENCODING-ASSUMED` | `vendors.csv` | The file is not UTF-8 and was read as Windows-1252. Check that the umlauts look right. |
| `DF-W-DECIMAL-COMMA` | `vendors.csv` | Numbers like `25.000,00`, read with a decimal comma. |

### The file types

| What | File endings | What awa reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Excel | `.xlsx`, `.xlsm` | The sheets, tables, columns and a totals row. |
| Tables as text | `.csv`, `.tsv` | The columns, the separator and the encoding, also numbers like `4.250,00`. |
| PDF | `.pdf` | The text. A scanned page has none, and awa says so; the `workspace` connector reads such pages with a vision model. |
| Word | `.docx` | The text and the tables. |
| Email | `.eml`, `.mbox` | Sender, subject, date, the start of the text and the names of attachments. |
| Data and text | `.json`, `.txt`, `.md` | The structure, or the text. |
| Database file | `.db`, `.sqlite` | The tables of a copy. To read a database where it is, add it as a system ([Connect systems](connect.md)). |
| Zip archive | `.zip` | The files inside, when every file in it is safe. |

awa looks at what is inside a file, not at its ending. A program renamed to `invoice.pdf` is refused. A file awa
cannot read, such as an old `.xls` or a picture, is listed with the reason. The web app takes up to 200 files, 50 MB
each and 500 MB in all.

### What the model sees

The model that designs your process never reads your files. It reads only a short **digest** of them. `--model-view`
prints exactly that digest. `--mask placeholders` replaces names, tax numbers and bank numbers with placeholders:

<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ awa data inspect data/vendors.csv --model-view --mask placeholders
...
Personal data is replaced by placeholders of the form <KIND_1>: the same value has the same placeholder in every file.
...
| Lieferantennr | Name | USt-IdNr | IBAN | Status | Bestelllimit_EUR |
| V-100 | <NAME_1> | <TAXID_1> | <IBAN_1> | aktiv | 25.000,00 |
| V-300 | <NAME_2> | <TAXID_2> | <IBAN_2> | gesperrt | 5.000,00 |
| V-400 | <NAME_3> | <TAXID_3> | <IBAN_3> | aktiv | 10.000,00 |
...
```

The same value gets the same placeholder in every file, so lines that belong together still match. `--mask drop`
leaves out the sample rows, so the model sees only the structure. In the web app, the switch **Hide personal data
from the AI** on the page **Data** does the same.

### What the mask covers

The mask applies to the digest that the design model sees. It replaces personal data in what the *design* model
reads: the digest of your files and the example rows of your systems. You still see everything, and the files are
never changed.

awa recognizes names, tax numbers, bank numbers, email addresses and phone numbers by their form. A name inside free
text may be missed.

The mask does not protect the running process. Agents that read your files through the file tools see the file
content unmasked at run time, and so do agents that read a system with its tools. Give an agent only the files it
needs, or use the redaction guardrail (`RegexRedactor.pii()` hides email addresses and IBANs, not names). See
[Where your data goes](#where-your-data-goes).

## Build on your files

Give `awa build` your description and the files. `--data` takes a file, a folder or a pattern, and you can repeat
it. This example uses the folder `invoice-files` from the tour:

<!-- guide:do cd . -->
<!-- guide:run model=files -->
```console
$ awa build "Supplier invoices arrive as PDF files. Check each invoice against the open purchase orders in purchase_orders.csv: the purchase order must be open and the amount must match. A matching invoice is released for payment. From 5,000 EUR the head of finance must approve the payment first." --out files-desk --data invoice-files --no-input
[profile] Reading your files
[profile] INV-2041.pdf: pdf (ok)
[profile] INV-2042.pdf: pdf (ok)
[profile] purchase_orders.csv: csv (ok)
[profile] Read 3 file(s): 1 table(s), 2 row(s), 0 warning(s), 0 unreadable
[design] Writing the acceptance tests, then the design
[design] The acceptance tests are written: 2 case(s)
[design] The blueprint 'invoice_check' is designed
[evaluate] Round 1: running the cases
[evaluate] Case small-invoice: passed
[evaluate] Case large-invoice: passed
[evaluate] Round 1: 2 of 2 cases pass
[write] Writing the project to files-desk
[write] The project is written
[done] Target reached
invoice_check: 2 of 2 eval cases pass (100%) on the local workspace after 1 round(s); target reached.
Project folder: files-desk
Where the data comes from:
  - Your files (CSV file, PDF document): your files (INV-2041.pdf, INV-2042.pdf, purchase_orders.csv), copied into the project (data/files/) and read there by the file tools; the originals are never changed.
    details: blueprint.yaml connectors: files: use workspace; root data/files; tools files_list_files, files_query_csv, files_read_pdf
  - Results folder (folder data/output/): where the process writes its results (data/output/ in the project folder); a person approves each write.
    details: blueprint.yaml connectors: output: use workspace; root data/output; tools output_write_file
Refinement: none (the traces show nothing to refine).
Model usage: 12 call(s) (design 2, evaluation 10, judges 0, repair 0), 12371 tokens.
Next: read README.md and CONNECT.md in the project folder.
```

What happens, in order:

1. awa reads the files (`[profile]`) and checks that your words fit them.
2. It writes the tests from the real rows and designs the process.
3. It runs the tests on copies of your files.

The project folder gets the copies, what awa found, and a `data:` section in `blueprint.yaml`:

<!-- guide:tree files-desk -->
```text
.env.example
.gitignore
CONNECT.md
README.md
blueprint.yaml
data/PROFILE.json
data/PROFILE.md
data/files/INV-2041.pdf
data/files/INV-2042.pdf
data/files/purchase_orders.csv
evals/cases.yaml
tests/test_tools.py
tools.py
```

The `data:` section lists every file with its [role](../reference/glossary.md#file-role) and what awa found in it.
`input` files are processed one by one, `reference` files are looked up, and `output` is where results go:

<!-- guide:contains files-desk/blueprint.yaml -->
```yaml
- name: purchase_orders
  path: data/files/purchase_orders.csv
  role: reference
  description: 'The open purchase orders: number, vendor, amount and status.'
  expect:
    columns:
    - po
    - vendor
    - amount
    - status
    header_row: 1
    decimal: .
    min_rows: 1
  handling: Look the purchase order up by its number; the amount must match.
```

The options for files (all options: [`awa build`](../reference/cli.md#awa-build)):

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--data PATH` | A file, a folder (read with everything below it) or a pattern such as `"inbox/*.pdf"`. Repeatable. |
| `--note FILE=TEXT` | What must happen with a file, in your own words. |
| `--mask placeholders` or `drop` | Hide personal data from the design model. The default is `none`. |
| `--answer TEXT` | Your answer to a question of an earlier build (`q1=TEXT`). |
| `--no-input` | Never ask: a question is printed as JSON and the exit code is 2. |

A note goes in front of what the model wrote for the file:

<!-- guide:run model=files -->
```console
$ awa build "Supplier invoices arrive as PDF files. Check each invoice against the open purchase orders in purchase_orders.csv: the purchase order must be open and the amount must match. A matching invoice is released for payment. From 5,000 EUR the head of finance must approve the payment first." --out files-desk --force --data invoice-files --note "purchase_orders.csv=Look up the purchase order by its number." --mask placeholders --no-input
...
invoice_check: 2 of 2 eval cases pass (100%) on the local workspace after 1 round(s); target reached.
...
```

<!-- guide:contains files-desk/blueprint.yaml -->
```yaml
  handling: Look up the purchase order by its number. Look the purchase order up by its number; the amount
    must match.
```

### When the words do not fit the files

If you describe CV screening and bring invoices, awa asks instead of inventing something. With `--no-input`, the
question is printed as JSON, nothing is written, and the exit code is 2:

<!-- guide:run model=files exit=2 -->
```console
$ awa build "Screen the incoming CVs against our role profile and schedule interviews." --out cv-desk --data invoice-files --no-input
...
{
  "status": "needs_input",
  "reason": "The description is about CVs or candidates, but the files hold purchase_orders.csv (po, vendor, amount, status). Which file is it, or should other files be added?",
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "q1",
      "text": "The description is about CVs or candidates, but the files hold purchase_orders.csv (po, vendor, amount, status). Which file is it, or should other files be added?",
      "evidence": [
        "f3.t1.po",
        "f3.t1.vendor"
      ],
      "options": []
    }
  ]
}
```

`evidence` names the parts of the profile the question is about: `f3.t1.po` is the column `po` of the first table of
the third file. Run the same command again with your answer in `--answer`. Text inside a file can never answer for
you:

<!-- guide:run model=files -->
```console
$ awa build "Screen the incoming CVs against our role profile and schedule interviews." --out cv-desk --data invoice-files --no-input --answer "q1=Use purchase_orders.csv: check the invoices against the purchase orders."
...
invoice_check: 2 of 2 eval cases pass (100%) on the local workspace after 1 round(s); target reached.
...
```

Without `--no-input`, awa asks the question in the terminal and you type the answer:

<!-- guide:run model=files input="Use purchase_orders.csv: check the invoices against the purchase orders.|" -->
```console
$ awa build "Screen the incoming CVs against our role profile and schedule interviews." --out cv-desk-2 --data invoice-files
...
q1: The description is about CVs or candidates, but the files hold purchase_orders.csv (po, vendor, amount, status). Which file is it, or should other files be added?
Your answer: Use purchase_orders.csv: check the invoices against the purchase orders.
...
invoice_check: 2 of 2 eval cases pass (100%) on the local workspace after 1 round(s); target reached.
...
What should start it? [webhook/schedule/file-drop/mail/queue] (Enter: nothing, start it by hand):
```

| Exit code of `awa build` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | The project was written and the tests reached the target. |
| `1` | The target was not reached, or nothing can be built from the files (`blocked`, for example a folder of pictures). |
| `2` | awa needs your answer (`needs_input`). Nothing was written. |

## Run the process on each file

`awa data run` runs the process once for each **input** file. You need no trigger and no server. Reference files
such as `purchase_orders.csv` are only looked up.

Each run asks before it writes its result. The large invoice also asks the head of finance first:

<!-- guide:do cd files-desk -->
<!-- guide:run model=files input="y|y|y" -->
```console
$ awa data run . --all
Approval needed:
{
...
}
Answer here: y approves the step; anything else rejects it.
Approve? [y/N] y
INV-2041.pdf: completed; wrote data/output/INV-2041.pdf/INV-2041.txt (runs/run_a02e274e7f8d.json)

Approval needed:
{
...
  "condition": "amount_eur >= 5000"
}
Answer here: y approves the step; anything else rejects it.
Approve? [y/N] y

Approval needed:
{
...
}
Answer here: y approves the step; anything else rejects it.
Approve? [y/N] y
INV-2042.pdf: completed; wrote data/output/INV-2042.pdf/INV-2042.txt (runs/run_7a32fa51d2f3.json)
```

Every run:

- works on a fresh copy of `data/`;
- writes only below `data/output/`, in a folder named after the input file;
- leaves a report in `runs/` with the file's fingerprint (`sha256`), what it was asked, the tool calls, the
  approvals, the outputs and the usage.

<!-- guide:tree files-desk/data/output -->
```text
INV-2041.pdf/INV-2041.txt
INV-2042.pdf/INV-2042.txt
```

<!-- guide:contains data/output/INV-2041.pdf/INV-2041.txt -->
```text
INV-2041: purchase order PO-7710 is open and the amount 1,180.00 EUR matches.
```

In a script, add `--no-input` so awa never asks. A run that needs an approval then ends **paused** with exit code 2.
`--json` prints the outcomes for a program, and `--file` picks files by name or pattern:

<!-- guide:run model=files exit=2 -->
```console
$ awa data run . --file "INV-2042.pdf" --json --no-input
[
  {
    "file": "INV-2042.pdf",
    "status": "paused",
    "answer": "",
    "error": "",
    "approvals": [
      "finance_approval"
    ],
    "tool_calls": [
      "files_read_pdf",
      "files_query_csv",
      "finance_approval"
    ],
    "outputs": [],
    "run_id": "run_cc5c156e55c7",
    "report": "runs/run_cc5c156e55c7.json",
    "usage": {
      "requests": 3,
      "total_tokens": 1632
    }
  }
]
A run is paused for an approval; run this command in a terminal to decide.
```

`awa data run` ends with exit code 0 when every run completed, 1 when a run failed, and 2 when a run is paused. The
limits options (`--max-requests`, `--max-duration` and the others of [Keep it running](operate.md#limits-and-costs))
apply to each run.

## Check that the files still fit

Files change: a supplier renames a column, a new export has another layout. `awa data check` tests the `data:`
section against the files in `data/files`, without a model:

<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ awa data check .
.: data matches (0 errors, 0 warnings)
```

Now a supplier renames the column `po`:

<!-- guide:do replace files-desk/data/files/purchase_orders.csv "po,vendor" "po_number,vendor" -->

<!-- guide:run exit=1 -->
```console
$ awa data check .
warning: data[2].path: data changed since the profile was written: 'data/files/purchase_orders.csv' differs from data/PROFILE.json; the files were profiled again
error: data[2].expect.columns[0]: column 'po' does not exist in 'data/files/purchase_orders.csv' (its columns: 'po_number', 'vendor', 'amount', 'status') [DF-V-003]
.: 1 error, 1 warning
```

The message names the entry of `data:` (`data[2]`, the third), the missing column and the columns the file has now.
`--json` gives the same for a program, and `awa validate` runs the same check.

To fix it, do one of these: put the old file back, change `expect:` in `blueprint.yaml`, or build again with
`--force`.

<!-- guide:do replace files-desk/data/files/purchase_orders.csv "po_number,vendor" "po,vendor" -->

<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ awa data check .
.: data matches (0 errors, 0 warnings)
```

## The tools agents read files with

You only need this section when you write or change a blueprint by hand. While a process runs, agents open files
with tools, one for each kind:

| Your file | The tool | What the agent gets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSV | `builtin:read_csv`, `builtin:query_csv` | Rows and columns; `query_csv` filters and adds up without reading everything. |
| Excel | `builtin:read_excel`, `builtin:query_excel` | Rows of one sheet; `header_row` skips a title block. |
| PDF | `builtin:extract_pdf_text` | The text of each page. |
| Word | `builtin:extract_docx_text` | Paragraphs and tables in reading order. |
| JSON | `builtin:json_query` | The part you ask for. |
| Text and Markdown | `builtin:read_file` | The text. |
| A folder | `builtin:list_files` | The names of the files in it. |

The file tools see only one folder, named in the blueprint. Absolute paths, `..`, hidden files such as `.env` and
anything outside are refused. A tool that writes, moves or deletes waits for approval:

```yaml
toolkits:
  files: {root: ./data}
```

### Example: an invoice inbox

The example `intake-desk` shows these tools at work. Its clerk reads each invoice and checks it against
`vendors.csv` and `purchase_orders.json` with rules in `tools.py`. Clean invoices are booked; the rest go on hold. A
booking above 10,000 EUR waits for a manager:

<!-- guide:do cd intake-desk -->
<!-- guide:run model=intake -->
```console
$ awa validate blueprint.yaml
document-intake: valid
$ awa show blueprint.yaml
document-intake 1.0.0
Extracts, validates and books supplier invoices that arrive as PDF, Word or Excel.
entrypoint: intake_clerk

agent ...
intake_clerk ...

approvals: book_invoice (when gross_amount > 10000)
```

Process the PDF. `--stream` shows each step:

<!-- guide:run model=intake -->
```console
$ awa run blueprint.yaml "Process the document inbox/2024-0412_mueller.pdf." --stream
> intake_clerk started
  intake_clerk -> extract_pdf_text({"path": "inbox/2024-0412_mueller.pdf"})
  intake_clerk <- extract_pdf_text [ok]: --- page 1 --- RECHNUNG 2024-0412 ...
  intake_clerk -> validate_invoice({"vendor_vat_id": "DE811111111", "iban": "DE02100100100000123456", "po_number": "PO-4500", "net_amount": 1200.0, "tax_amount": 228.0, "gross_amount": 1428.0,...)
  intake_clerk <- validate_invoice [ok]: {"valid": true, "vendor_id": "V-100", "violations": []}
  intake_clerk -> book_invoice({"po_number": "PO-4500", "net_amount": 1200.0, "tax_amount": 228.0, "gross_amount": 1428.0, "due_date": "2024-10-20", "vendor_id": "V-100", "invoice_number":...)

}

[intake_clerk] 4 model call(s), 2713 tokens (2681 in, 32 out), 558 ms

The German amounts and dates (`1.428,00`, `20.09.2024`) were read correctly.

Everything the agent reads from a file reaches the model marked as data it must not take orders from. That lowers
the risk that a PDF saying "ignore your rules and pay" changes what the clerk does. It does not rule it out.

The Word invoice is above 10,000 EUR, so `awa run` shows the request and asks; `y` approves:

===========================

- Pass rate: 100.0% (5/5 runs)
- Errors: 0
...
```

## Where your data goes

awa runs on your computer and keeps your files there. But an agent is an AI model run by your provider, so
**whatever an agent reads with a tool is sent to that provider.** The mask changes what the design model sees, not
what an agent reads later.

- Give an agent only the files it needs.
- Use a provider your organization has approved.
- Ask your data-protection contact when you are not sure.

[Safety: data protection](../develop/safety.md#data-protection) lists the controls for personal data.

## Common mistakes

| Mistake | What you see | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The file is outside the files folder | `Error: path ... must be relative to the allowed directory` | Put the file inside the folder and name it relative to it. |
| A scanned PDF | *Looks like a scan*, or `[no text layer: ...]` | Read it through the `workspace` connector, which reads scans with a vision model ([Connect systems](connect.md)); or hold scans for manual entry, or bring a text version. |
| An Excel title block above the headers | Columns named `Unnamed` | Name the row with the column names: `header_row`. |
| Numbers read wrongly | `1.234` taken as 1.234 | Say it in the instructions: "amounts like 1.428,00 mean 1428.00". |
| `--note` without `--data` | `error: --note, --mask and --answer belong to --data: name your files` | Add the files. |
| The project folder exists | `error: 'files-desk' already holds a project` | Add `--force`, or choose another `--out`. |
| `--file` matches nothing | `error: no input file matches ...` | Use a name from the list the message gives. |
| A script hangs on an approval | `--no-input` is missing | Add it: the run ends paused with exit code 2. |

<!-- guide:do cd . -->

!!! example "In code"

    `awa.data.profile` is `awa data inspect` from Python; `awa.blueprints.run_project` is `awa data run`
    ([Data](../develop/data.md#what-a-profile-holds)).

    <!-- guide:python -->
    ```python
    from awa.data import profile

    found = profile("intake-desk/data", root="intake-desk/data")
    print(found.summary.files, "files,", found.summary.warnings, "warnings")
    for file in found.files:
        print(file.path, file.kind, file.status)
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    6 files, 6 warnings
    inbox/2024-0412_mueller.pdf pdf ok
    inbox/88231_zuercher.docx docx ok
    inbox/ln-2024-17_meyer.xlsx xlsx ok
    inbox/scan_0001.pdf pdf ok
    purchase_orders.json json ok
    vendors.csv csv ok
    ```

<!-- source: guide/connect.md -->

# Connect systems

Use this page when your process must read from or write to one of your systems: a database, a web service, a mailbox
or a ticket tool. A [connector](../reference/glossary.md#connector) gives the agents tools for one system, such as
"find a customer" or "create a ticket". You give it an address and a key.

The shortest path: open the page **Connect** in the web app, or run `awa connect .` in the project folder. awa asks
for each missing setting, tests it and switches the process to the live system
([details](#enter-the-address-and-the-key)).

In the blueprint, a connector is a few lines. This one lets the agent `analyst` read a database:

```yaml
connectors:
  shop:
    use: sql
    env: {DATABASE_URL: SHOP_DATABASE_URL}
    read_only: true
agents:
  - name: analyst
    tools: [connector:shop.schema, connector:shop.query]
```

Two rules keep this safe:

- **Keys stay out of the blueprint.** The blueprint holds only the names of the settings. The values are in the file
  `.env` of the project folder, on your computer.
- **Changes wait for a person.** Reading runs directly. Anything that changes or sends something waits for approval,
  unless you switch that off for a connector with `requires_approval: false` (`awa validate` then warns).

## Two ways to connect a system

You can connect a system at two moments:

- **Before the build**, when you already know the system. The design then fits its real structure, as in
  [step 3 of the tour](tour.md#step-3-bring-your-files-and-your-ledger).
- **After the build**, when you want to try the process first, or when the process must change data in that system.
  Connecting changes only the entry under `connectors:` and `.env`; the agents and the tests stay. Then adjust the
  expected values of the eval cases to your real data and test again.

| | Before the build: page **Data**, or `awa data add-system` | After the build: page **Connect**, or `awa connect` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What awa does | Tests the system, saves its settings, reads its structure (tables and columns, or the operations of an API) | Saves the settings, tests the system, switches it from its stand-in to the live system |
| The design | Uses the real tables or operations | Was made on the **stand-in**: sample records awa wrote from your description |
| Changes to the system | None: the system gets no tool that changes data | Possible, and each one waits for a person |

## See what awa can connect to

<!-- guide:do cd . -->
<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ awa connectors list
NAME             CATEGORY       STABILITY  SETTINGS   TOOLS             TITLE
openapi          generic        core       1 missing  listed by system  OpenAPI (any documented REST API)
rest             generic        core       1 missing  1 read, 1 write   REST API
odata            generic        core       1 missing  4 read, 2 write   OData service
graphql          generic        core       1 missing  3 read, 1 write   GraphQL API
workspace        data           core       set        12 read, 5 write  Local workspace
sql              data           core       1 missing  2 read, 1 write   SQL database
web              web            core       set        2 read, 0 write   Web pages and search
smtp             communication  core       2 missing  0 read, 1 write   Email sending (SMTP)
...
```

- `STABILITY` is `core`, or `preview`: no stability promise, tested against fake connections.
- `SETTINGS` says `set` (the settings are there, the connection is not tested yet) or how many are missing.

The whole catalog:

| Connector | System | What the agents can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace` | The project folder (`data/`): the stand-in of every system | Files, CSV and Excel tables, PDF and Word, a SQLite database; writing *(approval)* |
| `sql` | SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL or MariaDB, SQL Server | Read the structure, query; change data *(approval)* |
| `openapi` | Any web API with an OpenAPI description | The operations the description lists |
| `rest` | Any web API with JSON | The operations you describe; send *(approval)* |
| `odata` | OData services, such as ERP and CRM systems | List, describe, query, read; create and update *(approval)* |
| `graphql` | Any GraphQL API | Describe, query; change *(approval)* |
| `web` | Web pages and search | Read a page or PDF; search the web |
| `smtp`, `imap` | Sending and reading email | Send *(approval)*; search and read messages |
| `webhook` | A chat channel or automation endpoint | Post *(approval)* |
| `outlook`, `sharepoint`, `teams` | Microsoft 365 *(preview)* | Mail, files and channels; see [Microsoft 365](microsoft-365.md) |
| `microsoft_graph` | Microsoft 365, broad and older *(preview)* | Prefer `outlook`, `sharepoint` and `teams` |
| `slack` | Slack *(preview)* | Read channels and threads; post *(approval)* |
| `jira` | Jira *(preview)* | Search and read issues; create issues and comments *(approval)* |

To see what one system needs, name it:

<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ awa connectors show jira
jira: Jira (ticketing)
  Search, read, create and comment on Jira issues.
  status: missing JIRA_URL, JIRA_EMAIL, JIRA_API_TOKEN
  variables:
    JIRA_URL                     not set    required  Address of your Jira site.
    JIRA_EMAIL                   not set    auth  Email address of the Jira account.
    JIRA_API_TOKEN               not set    auth  API token of that account.
    JIRA_TOKEN                   not set    auth  Personal access token (Jira Data Center).
  authentication (first complete one is used): JIRA_EMAIL + JIRA_API_TOKEN | JIRA_TOKEN
  tools:
    connector:jira.search_issues  Find issues with a JQL query (e.g. project = OPS AND status = 'In Progress').
    connector:jira.get_issue  Read one issue with its description and comments.
    connector:jira.create_issue [approval]  Create an issue.
    connector:jira.add_comment [approval]  Add a comment to an issue.
  setup: Create an API token at https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens.
  docs: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/
```

Read it like a form:

- `variables` are the settings to fill. awa shows whether each one is set, never its value.
- `authentication` says which combination of settings the system accepts.
- `tools` are what the agents get. `[approval]` marks the tools that wait for a person.

## Enter the address and the key

=== "Web app"

    Open the page **Connect**. Each system of your process has a card: **Live**, **Needs attention** (a setting is
    missing or not tested yet) or **Stand-in**.

    1. Fill in the fields. An address must start with `https://`; a key is hidden while you type and afterwards
       shows only *saved*.
    2. Press **Test connection**: one small, read-only call with what you typed, and the answer in plain words, for
       example *The system refused the key*. Nothing is saved.
    3. Press **Save and connect**: awa saves the values in `.env`, tests again and switches the system from its
       stand-in to the live one. **Go back to the stand-in** switches it back.

    To prepare a system before any process uses it, open **Set up**: under **External systems** every connector of the
    catalog has a card with its fields.

    ![The Set up page, the card of the system Jira opened: the three settings with hidden fields](../assets/screenshots/guide/b03-systems.png)

    --8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/b03-systems.legend.txt"

=== "Terminal"

    For a project from `awa build`, run `awa connect .` in the project folder. It asks for every missing setting
    (your typing is hidden), saves it, tests it and switches the project over. An empty answer skips a setting.
    Systems that are already connected are skipped the next time.

    To connect one database to any folder, give it a short name. Here the ledger of the tour plays the database,
    and `shop-desk` is a new folder:

    <!-- guide:run input="company-ledger.db" -->
    ```console
    $ awa connect shop-desk --database shop
    SHOP_DATABASE_URL (postgresql://, mysql://, mssql:// or SQLite file), hidden: 
    Test passed: SQLite database company-ledger.db is readable; 1 table(s) and view(s): invoices
    Saved SHOP_DATABASE_URL in shop-desk/.env

    Add this to blueprint.yaml (agents get the tools they list):

    connectors:
      shop:
        use: sql
        env: {DATABASE_URL: SHOP_DATABASE_URL}
        read_only: true   # only schema and query; no tool that changes data
    agents:
      - name: analyst
        tools: [connector:shop.schema, connector:shop.query]
    ```

    The test only lists table names; it reads no data.

### Database addresses

| Database | Address |
| --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL | `postgresql://reporting@db.example.com:5432/shop` |
| MySQL or MariaDB | `mysql://reporting:password@db.example.com/shop` |
| SQL Server | `mssql://reporting:password@db.example.com:1433/shop` |
| SQLite | The path of the file |

- PostgreSQL needs the `postgres` extra. MySQL, MariaDB and SQL Server need the `sql` extra. The double-click
  installer has both, and `awa doctor` says when one is missing.
- Ask for a login that may only **read**.
- Queries cannot change data. SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL refuse changes in the session. SQL Server relies on a check
  of the query text, so a SQL Server connector needs `accept_text_check: true`.

## A web service with a key

Many systems offer a web interface (a REST API) with a key. You do not need a ready-made connector: describe the
calls the agents need, and each one becomes a tool. This blueprint lets an agent find a customer in a CRM and add a
note:

<!-- guide:file crm-desk/blueprint.yaml -->
```yaml
name: crm-desk
description: Finds a customer in the CRM and adds a note.
connectors:
  crm:
    use: rest
    base_url_env: CRM_URL
    auth: {type: api_key, header: X-Api-Key, token_env: CRM_KEY}
    operations:
      - name: find_customer
        description: Find customers by name or email.
        path: /customers
        params: [{name: q, description: Name or email.}]
      - name: add_note
        description: Add a note to a customer.
        method: POST
        path: /customers/{id}/notes
        params:
          - {name: id, description: Customer id., in: path}
          - {name: text, description: The note., in: body}
agents:
  - name: account_manager
    description: Looks customers up and records notes.
    instructions: Find the customer with find_customer. When asked, add a note with add_note.
    tools: [connector:crm.find_customer, connector:crm.add_note]
```

awa tells you which settings are missing:

<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ cd crm-desk
$ awa validate blueprint.yaml
warning: connectors.crm: connector 'crm' is not configured: set CRM_URL, CRM_KEY (see 'awa connectors show crm --blueprint <file>'); its tools fail until then
crm-desk: valid with 1 warning(s) (tool names not checked; no tools.py beside it)
$ awa connectors show crm --blueprint blueprint.yaml
crm: REST API (generic)
  Any HTTP/JSON API: operations declared in the configuration, or generic get/send tools below the base URL.
  status: missing CRM_URL, CRM_KEY
  variables:
    CRM_URL                      not set    required  Base address of the REST API.
    CRM_KEY                      not set    auth  API key.
  tools:
    connector:crm.find_customer  Find customers by name or email.
    connector:crm.add_note [approval]  Add a note to a customer.
  setup: Set <NAME>_URL to the API's base address and the credentials of the auth option (default: <NAME>_TOKEN as a bearer token, or <NAME>_USERNAME and <NAME>_PASSWORD).
```

Put the address and the key into `crm-desk/.env`:

<!-- guide:file .env -->
```text
CRM_URL=https://crm.example.com/api
CRM_KEY=your-key-here
```

<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ awa connectors show crm --blueprint blueprint.yaml
crm: REST API (generic)
  Any HTTP/JSON API: operations declared in the configuration, or generic get/send tools below the base URL.
  status: variables set (not tested)
  variables:
    CRM_URL                      SET        required  Base address of the REST API.
    CRM_KEY                      SET        auth  API key.
  tools:
    connector:crm.find_customer  Find customers by name or email.
    connector:crm.add_note [approval]  Add a note to a customer.
  setup: Set <NAME>_URL to the API's base address and the credentials of the auth option (default: <NAME>_TOKEN as a bearer token, or <NAME>_USERNAME and <NAME>_PASSWORD).
$ awa validate blueprint.yaml
crm-desk: valid (tool names not checked; no tools.py beside it)
```

`variables set (not tested)` means both settings are there. To prove they work, make one small real call:
`awa connectors test crm --blueprint blueprint.yaml`. It ends with exit code 1 when it fails.

- The call is the operation named by `health:` on the connector, for example `health: find_customer`.
- Without `health:`, the test only checks that the tools are ready.
- `awa connectors test --all` tests every connector.

How to write `auth` for the common kinds of login:

| What the system wants | In `auth` |
| --- | --- |
| A key in a header | `{type: api_key, header: X-Api-Key, token_env: CRM_KEY}` |
| A key in the address (`?api_key=...`) | `{type: api_key, query: api_key, token_env: CRM_KEY}` |
| A bearer token | Nothing: set `<NAME>_TOKEN`. |
| A user name and a password | Nothing: set `<NAME>_USERNAME` and `<NAME>_PASSWORD`. |

A system with an OpenAPI (Swagger) description needs no `operations:` at all. Each operation of the description
becomes a tool:

```yaml
connectors:
  billing:
    use: openapi
    spec: specs/billing.yaml
    include: [list_invoices, get_invoice]
    health: list_invoices
```

## Connectors in a blueprint

Declare each system once under `connectors:`, then give agents its tools:

- `connector:<name>` gives every reading tool of the system.
- `connector:<name>.<operation>` gives one operation.

The name is yours. With `use:` you can have several instances of one connector, each with its own settings:

| Setting | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `use` | The catalog connector of a named instance. |
| `base_url` / `base_url_env` | The address, or the name of the setting that holds it. |
| `env` | Settings to read under other names, such as `{JIRA_URL: OPS_JIRA_URL}`. |
| `read_only: true` | Only the reading tools. |
| `include: [...]` | Only these operations. |
| `requires_approval: false` | Let writing tools run without approval (`awa validate` warns). |
| `timeout`, `retries` | Seconds per request; retries of temporary failures. |
| `allowed_hosts`, `allow_private_networks`, `allow_http` | Requests go only to the system's own address over `https://`; these allow more, for example a system inside your company network. |

Temporary failures are retried, and long lists are read page by page up to a limit. awa removes known credential
values and common credential formats from its answers, errors and logs. A tool you wrote that echoes a key back is
not covered.

Not covered by the catalog?

- The tools of an MCP server are added with `mcp:<server>` ([MCP](../develop/mcp.md)).
- For any other system, a developer writes a connector or a tool ([Connectors](../develop/connectors.md)).

## Common mistakes

| Mistake | What you see | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The key is in the blueprint | You can read it in the file | Move it to `.env` and name it with `token_env`. |
| `.env` is not in the folder you run awa in | `awa validate` warns that settings are not set | Go to the project folder. |
| The name in `.env` differs from what awa expects | `status: missing ...` although you entered it | Copy the name from `awa connectors show`. |
| `The connection test failed` | The system did not answer or refused the login | Check the address, the key and whether the system accepts connections from your computer (a VPN?). |
| `requests to internal networks are blocked` | The system is inside your company network | Set `allow_private_networks: true`, and `allow_http: true` if it has no TLS. |
| `.env` is shared or committed | The key is exposed | Never share it. The web app's download leaves it out; `.env.example` lists the names only. |

!!! example "In code"

    The catalog is a Python list too; a developer adds a connector of their own
    ([Write a connector](../develop/connectors.md#write-a-connector)).

    <!-- guide:python -->
    ```python
    from awa.connectors import list_connectors

    print(sorted(c.name for c in list_connectors() if c.category == "data"))
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    ['sql', 'workspace']
    ```

<!-- source: guide/microsoft-365.md -->

# Microsoft 365

Use this page when your process works with Microsoft 365 mail, files or Teams. awa reaches one Outlook mailbox, one
SharePoint site and one Teams channel. It also ships six ready-made processes on top of them that stop where a person
has to decide.

The shortest path to a running process:

1. Register one app in Microsoft Entra ([Step 1](#step-1-register-one-app)).
2. Run `awa connect microsoft`. It asks for the missing values, saves them in `.env` and checks them with read-only
   calls.
3. Copy one of [the processes](#the-processes), test it and run it
   ([Use a process with your own data](#use-a-process-with-your-own-data)).

In a blueprint, the connectors are one line each:

```yaml
connectors:
  mail: {use: outlook}
  files: {use: sharepoint}
agents:
  - name: assistant
    tools: [connector:mail.list_messages, connector:mail.read_message, connector:mail.create_reply_draft]
```

What keeps it safe:

- The mailbox, the site and the channel are settings in `.env`, never tool arguments. A model cannot wander into
  another mailbox, site or channel.
- Nothing is deleted. Every change (a reply draft, a move, an upload, a send) waits for a person.
- Mail and file contents reach the model as data, never as instructions.

!!! info "Preview"
    The connectors `outlook`, `sharepoint` and `teams` and the six processes are tested offline against a simulated
    Microsoft 365 with scripted models. The connectors were also read live on one test tenant. Writes, Excel edits,
    Teams and people search are not yet accepted live. Run them on a test mailbox and a test site, with a person
    checking the results, before you rely on them.

## The processes

The processes are in the awa folder under `examples/microsoft/`, one folder per family. Invented test data is in
`testdata/`.

| Folder | Process | What it does | What it can change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `briefings/` | `outlook-briefing` | Reads the unread mail and writes a briefing: ids, summaries, stated deadlines, suspicious mail | nothing |
| `briefings/` | `sharepoint-briefing` | Reads the documents of one approved folder and writes a briefing that names its sources | nothing |
| `sales/` | `sales-inbox` | Sorts customer requests: what is wanted, what is missing, how urgent, the next step | nothing |
| `sales/` | `sales-offer-preparation` | Prices each request from the approved price list, checks every number, leaves a **reply draft** | drafts in the mailbox |
| `administration/` | `administration-inbox` | Finds the responsible department and the deadline in the approved list, leaves a **reply draft** | drafts in the mailbox |
| `digest/` | `approved-digest` | Combines mail and documents into a digest and sends it to one internal reviewer after a person approves | one mail, after approval |

- **A reply draft is not sent.** Saving it waits for an approval in awa. Then a person opens it in Outlook, checks it
  and presses **Send**.
- **Only the digest can send**, and only to the domains you allow (`allowed_domains`).
- **Every schedule is switched off** (`enabled: false`) until the [acceptance](#acceptance-before-a-schedule) is
  done.

**The offer is checked by code, not by the model.**

- Prices, discount tiers, approval roles and tax rates come from queries of the price list (`price-list.xlsx` in the
  SharePoint folder `Approved`).
- The calculator does the arithmetic in whole cents.
- A missing quantity, an unknown product, another currency or an expired price gets no amount. The line goes to a
  question for the customer or to a person.

The administration process takes the department and the deadline from `responsibilities.xlsx`. It never drafts a
reply to a sensitive request (payroll, personnel, banking).

Each process ships a `cases.yaml` whose checks need no judge model. `python examples/microsoft/make_testdata.py OUT`
builds the workbooks and sample documents for a test site.

The processes run offline against the simulated Microsoft 365 that the repository's tests use:

```console
python -m pytest tests/examples/test_microsoft_processes.py
```

This proves that they build, run end to end, keep their limits and produce the expected numbers and routes. It does
not prove how a real model words a draft, nor your tenant's permissions. That is what the acceptance is for.

## Connect Microsoft 365

Register the app (step 1), then run `awa connect microsoft`. It:

1. shows which values are set (never the values);
2. asks for the missing ones, with your typing hidden, and saves them in `.env`;
3. checks everything with read-only calls;
4. prints the message for your administrator.

Each connector needs its own Microsoft Graph permission:

| Connector | Works in | Needs (Microsoft Graph permission) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `outlook` | one mailbox (`MS_MAILBOX`) | `Mail.ReadWrite` (drafts, mark, move); `Mail.Read` for read only; `Mail.Send` only to send |
| `sharepoint` | one site (`MS_SITE_URL`) | `Sites.Selected` and a role `read` or `write` on that one site |
| `teams` | one channel | nothing for a Workflows webhook; delegated `ChannelMessage.Send` and `ChannelMessage.Read.All` for a signed-in user |

### Step 1: register one app

1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center: **Entra ID**, **App registrations**, **New registration**. Name it `awa`, keep
   "Accounts in this organizational directory only", choose **Register**.
2. Copy the **Application (client) ID** and the **Directory (tenant) ID** from the overview.
3. **Certificates & secrets**: a new client secret of 12 months or less, and copy its **Value** at once (not the
   Secret ID). Or upload a certificate, which Microsoft recommends and some tenants require; awa then reads
   `AZURE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH` (a PEM file with key and certificate, or `.pfx`) and signs a short-lived proof per
   sign-in, so the key never leaves the computer.

```bash
AZURE_TENANT_ID=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
AZURE_CLIENT_ID=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET=paste-the-secret-value-here
```

`awa check microsoft` warns 30 days before a certificate expires; an expired secret answers "the client secret has
expired".

### Outlook mail

Add the application permission **`Mail.ReadWrite`** and **Grant admin consent**. Granted this way it reaches every
mailbox of the company, so an Exchange administrator narrows it to one mailbox with Exchange RBAC for Applications and
then revokes the tenant-wide consent (a change can take up to 2 hours):

```powershell
Connect-ExchangeOnline
New-ServicePrincipal -AppId <client id> -ObjectId <enterprise application object id> -DisplayName "awa"
New-ManagementScope -Name "awa-mailboxes" -RecipientRestrictionFilter "PrimarySmtpAddress -eq 'support@company.example'"
New-ManagementRoleAssignment -App <enterprise application object id> -Role "Application Mail.ReadWrite" -CustomResourceScope "awa-mailboxes"
```

Then set `MS_MAILBOX=support@company.example` in `.env` (a shared mailbox works the same) and run
`awa connectors test outlook`. The tools: `list_messages`, `search_messages`, `read_message` and `get_attachment`
read; `create_reply_draft`, `reply_to_message`, `send_mail`, `move_message` and `mark_processed` wait for approval.
A reply is a draft first and sent second; when Microsoft's answer to a send is lost, awa does not try again (you could
send two emails) and names the draft's id instead.

### SharePoint files and Excel

Add the application permission **`Sites.Selected`** and grant consent; the app can then reach no site at all. A
