Read **What went wrong** first. The indentation shows who asked whom, the brackets what each agent used, `->` how a
call ended. `!` lines mark a limit, an error or a refused call where it happened. `awa run` writes a trace when you
ask, and `--trace-level full` adds what was asked, answered and returned:

<!-- guide:do cd invoice-desk -->
<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ awa run blueprint.yaml "Please release invoice INV-2041 for payment." --trace trace-1.jsonl --trace-level full
trace written to trace-1.jsonl; read it with: awa runs trace trace-1.jsonl
Invoice INV-2041 from Nordwind Office GmbH (1,180.00 EUR) is released for payment.

[invoice_desk] 4 model call(s), 1121 tokens (1062 in, 59 out), 134 ms
$ awa runs trace trace-1.jsonl
Trace of run run_8c1f2a47e90b4d6f8a3b5c71d2e9f046
  file trace-1.jsonl (level full)
Result: finished
Totals: 4 model calls, 1,121 tokens (1,062 in, 59 out), time 134 ms
        agents 3, tool calls 2 (0 only hand work to other agents), delegations 0, consultations 0, handoffs 0, approvals 0 asked / 0 answered

workflow invoice_desk  [no model calls, 134 ms]
  input: Please release invoice INV-2041 for payment.
  agent invoice_checker  [2 model calls, 506 tokens, 76 ms]
    input: Please release invoice INV-2041 for payment.
    tool invoice_ledger_query {"query": "SELECT supplier, po_number, amount_eur, status FROM invoices WHERE invoice_id = ?", "parameters": ["INV-2041"]} -> ok (9 ms)
...
    said: Invoice INV-2041 from Nordwind Office GmbH: 1,180.00 EUR, purchase order PO-7710, status open.
  agent payment_clerk  [2 model calls, 615 tokens, 41 ms]
    input: Invoice INV-2041 from Nordwind Office GmbH: 1,180.00 EUR, purchase order PO-7710, status open.
    tool finance_approval {"invoice_id": "INV-2041", "amount_eur": 1180.0} -> ok (2 ms)
      result: {"approved": true, "invoice_id": "INV-2041", "amount_eur": 1180.0}
    said: Invoice INV-2041 from Nordwind Office GmbH (1,180.00 EUR) is released for payment.
  output: Invoice INV-2041 from Nordwind Office GmbH (1,180.00 EUR) is released for payment.

Note: no prices, so no cost. Add `prices:` to the blueprint or pass --prices FILE.
```

**A full trace contains the personal data of the run**: use it to find a problem, then delete the file.
`AWA_TRACE_LEVEL` (`off`, `summary`, `full`) sets the level for the worker and the server. Every error message starts
with `error:` and ends with what to do; `awa --verbose` before a command prints the technical details.

The same runs in the browser, with every tool call's input and output, are in [Langfuse](langfuse.md):

![Langfuse: the tool call invoice_ledger_query of the invoice checker, with the SQL query and the invoice number INV-2042 as input and the ledger row as output](../assets/screenshots/tracing-tool-call.png)

*A tool call with the arguments the agent chose and what came back.*

| You see | Look at | Usually |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `credentials ABSENT` or an authentication error | `awa doctor` | The key is not set in the folder you work in. |
| A run waits and nothing happens | `awa runs list --status waiting` | An approval waits for a person. |
| Nothing starts | `awa trigger list`, is the worker running? | The worker is not running, or the folder or schedule is not what you think. |
| A run costs too much or takes long | `awa runs trace RUN` | One agent loops, or one step is slow. |
| A wrong answer | `awa run ... --trace FILE --trace-level full`, then `awa runs trace FILE` | A tool returned something unexpected, or an instruction is unclear. |

## When many people depend on it

On one computer everything is in `.awa`. When several computers share the work, or there are many runs, keep the runs
in PostgreSQL:

1. Set `AWA_POSTGRES_DSN` in `.env`, or pass `--dsn` to `awa worker`, `awa serve` and `awa runs`.
2. Test the connection with `awa doctor --check-postgres`.

Then `awa serve` only receives web requests, and workers on as many computers as you like run everything else. Ask
your IT team for this list:

- [ ] The worker runs as a service that starts with the computer and restarts when it stops.
- [ ] The runs are in a database with backups, or `.awa` is on a disk that is backed up.
- [ ] The keys are in a protected `.env`, not in the blueprint.
- [ ] `limits:` are set, and `notify:` points to a channel somebody reads.
- [ ] Someone answers the approvals, and `sla: approval_within` escalates the ones nobody answers.
- [ ] The [production checklist](../develop/production.md) is read.

To back up, copy the project folder with `.awa`. To start clean, stop the worker and the web app and delete `.awa`:
waiting runs are lost, the blueprint, the tests, the data and `.env` stay.

## Common mistakes

| Mistake | What you see | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `awa runs` in the wrong folder | `No process run ... in .awa\awa.db` | Go to the project folder, or pass `--store`. |
| The worker is not running | Runs stay `queued` | Start it: `awa worker blueprint.yaml`. |
| A retry of a run that hit a limit | It fails again | Raise the limit, drop the file again. |
| No limits on an automatic process | `awa validate` warns | Add `limits:`. |
| `max_cost` without `prices:` | An error that prices are missing | Add `prices:` for every model the system uses. |
| `No trace for ...` | Wrong folder, or tracing was off | Run in the project folder, or pass `--traces DIR`. |

!!! example "In code"

    `awa.automation` is what `awa worker` and `awa serve` run, for any awa system in Python
    ([Serving: jobs on your own queue](../develop/serving.md#jobs-on-your-own-queue)). Here a second event with the same business key starts no second run:

    <!-- guide:python -->
    ```python
    import asyncio

    from awa import Agent
    from awa.automation import Automation, RetryPolicy
    from awa.testing import FakeChatModel

    clerk = Agent("clerk", instructions="Book supplier invoices.", model=FakeChatModel(["Booked RE-17."]))
    invoices = Automation(clerk, input="Book invoice {payload.invoice_no}.", dedup="{payload.invoice_no}",
                          retry=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=3, initial="1m"))

    async def main() -> None:
        first = await invoices.submit({"invoice_no": "RE-17"})
        again = await invoices.submit({"invoice_no": "RE-17"})
        await invoices.run_pending()
        run = await invoices.store.get(first.run.id)
        print(run.status, run.output, first.run.id == again.run.id)

    asyncio.run(main())
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    succeeded Booked RE-17. True
    ```

<!-- source: guide/langfuse.md -->

# Langfuse

Langfuse is an open-source tracing tool that you can run on your own computer. Connect awa to it, and you see every
run in the browser: each agent, model call, tool call and approval, with its time, tokens and cost.

For a single run, `awa runs trace` in the terminal is enough ([Keep it running](operate.md#read-a-trace)). Use
Langfuse when you want the history: compare runs, follow a thread over several runs, or show a colleague what an agent
did.

Four lines in the `.env` of a project folder switch it on:

```text
AWA_LANGFUSE_TRACING=true
LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-...
LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-...
LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000
```

With them, `awa run`, `awa chat`, `awa eval`, `awa serve`, `awa worker` and `awa build` send each run to Langfuse.
awa needs no Langfuse package for it, only the `langfuse` extra of awa.

## Start Langfuse on your computer

Langfuse runs with Docker (Docker Desktop on Windows and macOS) and needs at least 4 GB of memory.

1. Make a new folder outside the awa folder. Download Langfuse's Docker Compose file into it; the command for your
   system is on the [Langfuse self-hosting page](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/docker-compose).
2. In that folder, run awa's helper, then start Langfuse. The helper replaces the placeholder passwords and binds
   every port to this computer. The first start downloads the images and takes longer.

    ```console
    mkdir langfuse-local
    cd langfuse-local
    python <the awa folder>/examples/observability/langfuse_local.py
    docker compose up -d
    ```

3. The helper wrote two files. Keep both in that folder:
    - `.env` holds the passwords of the databases, your login and the project's keys;
    - `awa-langfuse.env` holds the four lines above, with your keys.
4. Copy the four lines of `awa-langfuse.env` into the `.env` of your project.
5. Check the connection. `OK langfuse server answered and accepted the keys` means it works:

    ```console
    awa doctor --check-langfuse
    ```

6. Run anything. Without a model key, `python <the awa folder>/examples/observability/trace_demo.py` sends a scripted
   team run.
7. Open `http://localhost:3000`, sign in and choose **Tracing**. The run is there a few seconds after it ends.

## What Langfuse receives

By default Langfuse receives names, ids, tokens, cost, timing, errors and the metadata of each run. It receives **no
prompt, answer or tool data**.

`AWA_LANGFUSE_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true` in the project's `.env` sends them too, as in the pictures below. Do that only
where the data may be stored in Langfuse. Credentials and personal data such as email addresses and IBANs are masked
before sending, but names and free text are not recognized as personal data.

## What you see

The pictures show a run of the invoice desk of the [tour](tour.md) for invoice INV-2042. It was sent with a scripted
model (`scripts/langfuse_showcase.py`) and with content capture on. The invoice checker reads the ledger, the payment
clerk's release waits for the head of finance, and the run continues after the approval.

**One run as a tree.** The workflow, both agents nested under it, and every model and tool call, with the run's time,
cost and tokens at the top:

![Langfuse showing the run of invoice INV-2042 as a tree: the workflow, the invoice checker and the payment clerk with their model and tool calls, and the run's time, cost and tokens](../assets/screenshots/tracing-tree.png)

**A model call.** The answer, the time, the tokens and the cost of one call. The full prompt of a call is not sent.
The input of each agent and every tool result are sent, so you can follow what the model knew:

![Langfuse: the model call of the invoice checker with its answer, its time, its tokens and its cost](../assets/screenshots/tracing-model-call.png)

**A tool call.** The arguments the agent chose and what the tool returned. A wrong argument here explains most wrong
answers:

![Langfuse: the tool call invoice_ledger_query of the invoice checker, with the SQL query and the invoice number INV-2042 as input and the ledger row as output](../assets/screenshots/tracing-tool-call.png)

**The approval and the decision.** The run stops at the approval request with the exact values. When the person
decides, it continues as a second trace of the same thread; [Approvals](approvals.md#see-an-approval-in-langfuse)
shows both. awa sends the thread of a run as its Langfuse session, so the paused run and its resumption read as one
story under **Sessions**.

## Find a run again

Every observation carries the metadata of its run. Type these into the search bar of **Tracing**:

| Search | Finds |
| --- | --- |
| `metadata.run_id:...` | One run; for a run of `awa worker`, the `proc_...` id that `awa runs list` shows. |
| `metadata.thread_id:thread_...` | Every run of one thread. |
| `metadata.blueprint:invoice-desk` | The runs of one blueprint. |
| `metadata.tenant:acme` | The runs of one tenant. |
| `metadata.agent_role:orchestrator` | The agents with that role. |
| `level:ERROR` | Failed tool calls and failed runs; `level:WARNING` marks a tool call that waits for approval. |

## Good to know

- **Langfuse is free when you run it yourself.** Tracing, sessions, users, cost and token tracking, dashboards and the
  API are in its MIT-licensed core.
- **The cost** of a model call comes from Langfuse's own price list for the models it knows. For other models, give
  awa your prices (`prices:` in the blueprint).
- **The model name** the provider reports is sent with each call. With Azure OpenAI it can contain the name of your
  deployment, so mask it before you share a screenshot.
- **Stop Langfuse** with `docker compose down` in its folder. `docker compose down -v` also deletes all traces.
- awa sends keys and traces over `https`, or over plain `http` only to a server on this computer.

## Common mistakes

| awa says | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `Langfuse keys are not set` | The four lines are not in the `.env` of the folder you run awa in. |
| `cannot use Langfuse: /api/public/health: ...` | Langfuse is not running or still starting: `docker compose ps` in its folder. |
| `the keys were rejected` | The keys belong to another project; copy them again from `awa-langfuse.env`. |
| `plain http on another computer` | Use the `https` address of your Langfuse. |
| A run is not there | Wait a few seconds, and check the time range at the top right of the page. |
| You see no prompts or answers | Content capture is off by default: add `AWA_LANGFUSE_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true`. |

!!! example "In code"

    `connect_langfuse` does the same as the setting from your own code, and needs the running Langfuse and its keys
    in the environment ([Observability](../develop/observability.md#langfuse)):

    ```python
    from awa.observability import connect_langfuse

    langfuse = connect_langfuse(capture_content=False, metadata={"blueprint": "invoice-desk"})
    ```

<!-- source: guide/web-app.md -->

# The web app

The web app takes you through a process in the browser, one page per step: from your description and your files to a
system that you check, test, connect and start. awa does the work that can be automated and checked; on each page you
decide what is right for your process. Use it when you prefer buttons and forms to a terminal.

Start it for a project folder:

```console
awa ui --project invoice-desk
```

awa prints a link and opens it in your browser. Keep the terminal open: closing it stops the web app.

The app works on one [project folder](../develop/project-folder.md), the same folder that the commands and
`awa.load` read, so you can switch between the web app and the terminal at any time. The [guided tour](tour.md)
walks through every page with one example; this page describes each page on its own.

The options you may need:

| Option of `awa ui` | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--project DIR` | The project folder, created when missing (default: the current folder). |
| `--port N` | The port (default 8765; a free one when it is taken). |
| `--no-browser` | Only print the link. |
| `--example ID` | Open a shipped example as a new project first ([Examples](examples.md)). |

The others are in the [command reference](../reference/cli.md#awa-ui); for `--allow-remote`, read
[Is it safe?](#is-it-safe) first.

## The pages

The pages are listed at the top of the window. Go through them in order the first time; later, jump to any page.
Every page starts with a box **What happens here** that sums up its section below.

| Page | What you do there | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Set up](#set-up) | Tell awa which AI model to use. | The key in `.env`, never shown again. |
| [Data](#data) | Bring the files your process works on, and the systems it reads. Optional. | Copies of your files, read and described; systems tested and declared. |
| [Describe](#describe) | Write the process in your own words and let awa build it. | A draft: `blueprint.yaml`, eval cases, the result of the test rounds. |
| [Review](#review) | Check what awa designed. | You know who does what and what waits for a person. |
| [Connect](#connect) | Enter the addresses and keys of your systems and test them. | Systems switched from stand-ins to live. |
| [Test](#test) | Run the eval cases. | Which cases pass, and why a case fails. |
| [Try it](#try-it) | Talk to the system and answer its approvals. | Answers, and the approval card before a gated step. |
| [Use it](#use-it) | Add triggers, try them on a sample, see the runs. | The command that keeps the system running. |
| [Approvals](#approvals) | Answer runs that wait for your OK. | Waiting runs continue or stop. |
| [Assistant](#hand-the-project-to-a-coding-assistant) | Write a brief for a coding assistant. | `BRIEF.md` with the process, the files and ready prompts. |

The pictures come from the invoice desk of the [guided tour](tour.md); a step number in a legend is a step of the
tour. Each section ends with a collapsed picture of the whole window.

!!! info "Preview"
    The web app works and is tested, but its pages and options may still change in a minor release ([Stability](../about/stability.md)).

## Set up

**Purpose:** tell awa which AI model to use and how to reach your external systems.

- **You enter:** under **AI model**, open the card of your provider and fill in its fields: a **key** (hidden while
  you type), an **address** for a provider that needs one (it must start with `https://`), and optionally the model
  as `provider:model` under *Which model should awa use?*. Under **External systems**, the settings of a connector
  of the catalog.
- **In the background:** **Save and continue** checks the form of each value and writes the values into `.env` in
  the project folder, readable only by you. The key is not tried here. The first real run calls the model, or
  `awa doctor --check-models` in a terminal.
- **Result:** the provider card says **Ready**. A saved value shows only as *Saved*; awa never shows it again.
- **If something goes wrong:**
    - *No key for the AI model is set up yet* (on another page): enter the key here.
    - *Your AI provider did not accept the key*: check the key and, for Azure OpenAI, the endpoint.
    - *The AI service does not know this model*: check the model name (for Azure, the deployment name).

![The Set up page: the card of the AI provider opened with a hidden key field, and the optional field for the model](../assets/screenshots/guide/a02-setup.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a02-setup.legend.txt"

In a terminal: `awa setup` asks for the provider and the key with hidden input and writes `.env`
([Set up a project](setup.md)).

??? note "The whole window"
    ![The Set up page: the card of the provider Anthropic opened with its hidden key field, and the cards of the other providers, not set up yet](../assets/screenshots/ui-setup.png)

## Data

**Purpose:** show awa what your process works on, so it designs on your real data instead of inventing some. This
page is optional: with **Skip: describe your process without files or systems**, awa writes small sample records
([stand-ins](../reference/glossary.md#stand-in)) from your description.

- **You enter:**
    - Under **Files**, drop documents or a whole folder (Excel, CSV, PDF, Word, email, JSON, text, SQLite, or a zip
      of them), or press **Choose files** or **Choose a folder**.
    - Under each file, a note in your own words in **What should happen with this data?**.
    - Under **External systems**, **Add an external system**: the kind, your name for it and its fields.
- **In the background:** each file is copied into `data/files` (your originals are never changed) and read without
  a model: its kind, columns, number and date formats, and what to watch. For a system, **Test connection** makes
  one small read-only call and saves nothing. **Test and save** saves its settings in `.env`, declares it in
  `data/SYSTEMS.json` and reads its structure (tables and columns, or the operations of an API). It reads no rows,
  unless you allow up to 3 example rows per table.
- **Result:** one card per file in plain words, such as *Looks like a scan*, and each system marked **Live,
  read-only**. The design and the test runs read the system live.
- **If something goes wrong:**
    - *Could not be read*: open the file yourself and bring a good copy.
    - *Looks like a scan*: the pages are pictures; see [Your files](files.md).
    - A file whose ending does not match its content is refused: export it again.
    - The limits are 200 files, 50 MB per file and 500 MB in all.
    - *The connection test failed*: check the address and the key, or ask for a read-only login.

![The Data page: the switch for personal data, the box for the files, the three copied files, a card for each file and the note under the purchase orders](../assets/screenshots/guide/a03-data.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a03-data.legend.txt"

![The form Add an external system: the kind SQL database, the name Invoice ledger, SQLite file, the hidden path, the Test connection button and the result](../assets/screenshots/guide/a03-systems-test.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a03-systems-test.legend.txt"

More on this page:

- **Hide personal data from the AI** (at the top) replaces names, IBANs and email addresses with placeholders in
  what the design model reads. Agents that read your data while they run see it unmasked
  ([What the mask covers](files.md#what-the-mask-covers)).
- **Remove** deletes a copy (press twice to confirm). **Analyze all again** reads every file again.
- **Start from an example** opens a shipped example in a new project folder next to the current one, with its files,
  its description and its eval cases.

In a terminal: `awa data inspect` and `awa data add-system` ([Your files](files.md), [Connect systems](connect.md)).

??? note "The whole window"
    ![The Data page: the cards of the copied invoices INV-2041 and INV-2042, each read, with the start of its text and the box What should happen with this data?](../assets/screenshots/ui-data.png)

    ![The card of the declared Invoice ledger: Live, read-only, the table invoices with its columns and the saved address, and below it the form Add an external system](../assets/screenshots/ui-systems.png)

## Describe

**Purpose:** turn your description into a first draft of the system, with eval cases that show whether the draft
fits.

- **You enter:** under **Your process**, what happens: what comes in, who checks or decides what, the rules with
  their numbers, and what comes out ([What a good description says](describe.md#what-a-good-description-says)).
  Leave **Test and repair it automatically** on.
- **In the background:** **Create my system** reads your data and writes eval cases from your words. Then it designs
  the agents against them, runs the cases on sample data, and repairs a failing design in up to three rounds. Five
  steps are ticked as they finish; if you reload the page, it picks up where it was. With a real model this usually
  takes a few minutes and costs tokens.
- **Result:** the project folder holds `blueprint.yaml`, `evals/cases.yaml`, `tools.py` and a `README.md` with the
  assumptions awa made. The page says what was built, how many cases pass, and where the data comes from (the data
  map).
- **If something goes wrong:**
    - *Describe your process in a few sentences first*: the box is empty.
    - *This folder already has a system*: creating a new one replaces it.
    - The target is not reached: read the failing cases, add the missing detail to the description and build again.

![The Describe page: your files and your ledger from step 3, the description in the large box, the switch for automatic testing and the Create my system button](../assets/screenshots/guide/a04-describe-before.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a04-describe-before.legend.txt"

![The Describe page after the build: the five steps ticked, the three eval cases that pass, the result in plain words and the data map with the live ledger](../assets/screenshots/guide/a04-describe-after.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a04-describe-after.legend.txt"

The cases come from your description, so "3 of 3 pass" says that the draft fits them. Whether they are the right
cases, you check on [Review](#review) and [Test](#test).

**Suggest patterns** proposes up to three ways for the agents to work together, from the words of your description,
without a model call. **Let my model rank them** adds one model call that orders them. **Test the proposals** drafts
a system per pattern, runs the same eval cases through each, and shows the results side by side, with a cap on model
calls. Nothing is saved until you press **Use this pattern**.

![The suggested patterns for the invoice desk: the card Fixed steps in a row with its diagram, when it fits, its roles and what to watch out for](../assets/screenshots/ui-patterns.png)

*Suggest patterns proposes ways for the agents to work together, from your words.*

In a terminal: `awa build "<process>" --data <folder>` ([Describe a process](describe.md)).

??? note "The whole window"
    ![The Describe page after a build: the five steps ticked, the three eval cases that pass, and the result: awa built invoice_desk, 3 of 3 eval cases pass](../assets/screenshots/ui-describe.png)

## Review

**Purpose:** check what awa designed before anything runs, and change it where it does not match how the work is
really done.

- **You read:** how the work flows (a diagram), each agent with its tools (*asks you first* marks a tool that waits
  for a person), **where the data comes from** (each source *Live*, *Your file (copy)*, *Stand-in* or *Results
  folder*, and what each agent reads and writes), and the eval cases.
- **You change:** **Edit the design (for advanced users)** shows the blueprint as text. **Check** lists the problems;
  **Check and save** saves only a design without errors.
- **Result:** you know who does what, what each agent reads and which step waits for a person.
- **If something goes wrong:**
    - *Not saved: fix the problems marked Must fix first*: each problem names the line; see
      [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#building-and-blueprints).
    - An approval you expected is missing: add it under `approvals:` ([Approvals](approvals.md)).

![The Review page: the flow diagram, the two agents with the finance approval marked asks you first, the data map with the live ledger, and the eval cases](../assets/screenshots/guide/a05-review.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a05-review.legend.txt"

In a terminal, with the approval rule as it stands in `blueprint.yaml`:

```console
awa validate blueprint.yaml
awa show blueprint.yaml
```

```yaml
approvals:
  - tool: finance_approval
    when: amount_eur >= 5000
```

??? note "The whole window and the editor"
    ![The Review page of the invoice desk: the work flows from invoice_checker to payment_clerk, the tool finance_approval is marked asks you first, and the invoice ledger is live](../assets/screenshots/ui-review.png)

    ![The blueprint editor on the Review page with the buttons Check and Check and save](../assets/screenshots/ui-edit-blueprint.png)

## Connect

**Purpose:** switch every system that still works on a stand-in to the live system, so the result runs on your real
data.

- **You enter:** each system has a card: *Live*, *Needs attention* (a setting is missing or not tested) or
  *Stand-in*. Press **Connect the live system**, then fill in its fields.
- **In the background:** **Test connection** makes one small read-only call. **Save and connect** saves the values
  in `.env`, tests again and switches the system from its stand-in to the real one. **Go back to the stand-in**
  switches it back.
- **Result:** every system the agents use is *Live*, or you know which one is not.
- **If something goes wrong:**
    - *The connection test failed*: the message names the cause. Check the address and the key, and the VPN for a
      system in your company network.
    - *These tools of the stand-in have no counterpart in the live system and were removed*: the live system offers
      fewer operations; check the agents on Review.

    More: [Connect systems](connect.md).

![The Connect page: one live system, the card of the Invoice ledger marked Live, and why: it was declared under Your data](../assets/screenshots/guide/a06-connect.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a06-connect.legend.txt"

In a terminal: `awa connect .` asks for every missing setting with hidden input.

??? note "The whole window"
    ![The Connect page: 1 of 1 live, the invoice ledger declared on the Data page with its saved address](../assets/screenshots/ui-connect.png)

## Test

**Purpose:** know, with numbers, whether the system does what the process needs.

- **You enter:** nothing; press **Run all tests** to run every case. To change a case, edit what it sends and press
  **Save and run this case**.
- **In the background:** every eval case runs against the system. Systems that are not connected yet answer from
  their stand-in. Each check of a case is scored, and its approvals are answered as the case says.
- **Result:** *Passed*, *Failed* or *Could not run* per case, and its answer. For a failed case you see the check
  that failed and why.
- **If something goes wrong:**
    - *No eval cases yet*: create the system on Describe with testing switched on.
    - **Could not run**: the message names the key, the limit or the connection.
    - A case passes on sample data and fails on real data: change its expected values ([Test and improve](test.md)).

![The Test page: the button Run all tests, the result 3 of 3 eval cases passed with the meter full, and the card of an eval case with what it sends, its files and its result](../assets/screenshots/guide/a07-test.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a07-test.legend.txt"

In a terminal, repeated three times to see [pass^k](../reference/glossary.md#pass-k):

```console
awa eval blueprint.yaml evals/cases.yaml --repetitions 3
```

??? note "The whole window"
    ![The Test page: 3 of 3 eval cases passed, and the card of eval case 1 with what it sends](../assets/screenshots/ui-test.png)

## Try it

**Purpose:** work with the system yourself, step by step, and see the approvals before you rely on them.

- **You enter:** a message, or one of **Try one of these** (requests from your eval cases); then **Send**. **Stop**
  ends the run at once. **New thread** starts a new conversation.
- **In the background:** the system runs with the blueprint's limits. Before a step marked *asks you first*, it stops
  and saves its state.
- **Result:** each step appears as a plain sentence. Before a gated step, the card **Please check before this
  happens** shows what will happen, the values and why you are asked:
    - **Approve** lets it go ahead.
    - **Say no** stops it.
    - **Tell the agent why** is a note that the agent reads.
- **If something goes wrong:**
    - *No AI model is set up yet, so the system cannot answer*: enter the key on Set up.
    - *The AI service is busy right now*: wait a minute and try again.
    - *That was too much text for the model at once*: use a shorter message or smaller files.

![The Try it page: the example requests, the steps of the system in plain words, the card that asks for your OK with the values and the reason, and the buttons Approve and Say no](../assets/screenshots/guide/a08-try-approval.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a08-try-approval.legend.txt"

![The conversation after the approval: the step that ran, the line You approved and the answer that invoice INV-2042 is released for payment](../assets/screenshots/guide/a08-try-answer.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a08-try-answer.legend.txt"

In a terminal: `awa chat blueprint.yaml` asks `approve? [y/N]` before a gated step.

??? note "The whole window"
    ![Try it: the card Please check before this happens for invoice INV-2042 and 7,450.00 EUR, why you are asked, and the buttons Approve and Say no](../assets/screenshots/ui-approval.png)

    ![Try it after the approval: the steps that ran, You approved, and the answer that invoice INV-2042 is released for payment](../assets/screenshots/ui-run.png)

## Use it

**Purpose:** put the system to work. See what starts it, try a trigger once on a sample, follow the runs, and get the
one command that keeps it running after you close the window.

- **You enter:** **Add another trigger**. Under **What starts it**, choose the kind (`schedule`, `webhook`,
  `file-drop`, `mail` or `queue`) and its settings, then fill in **What the system should do with each one** and
  press **Add this trigger**. **Run it now with a sample** takes the values that one event would carry.
- **In the background:** the trigger is written into `blueprint.yaml`. A sample run runs once, for real, on this
  computer. A step that needs your OK waits under **Waiting for your OK**.
- **Result:** the page shows:
    - **Is it running?**: whether an `awa worker` or `awa serve` waits for events;
    - **Waiting for your OK**;
    - **What starts it**: each trigger as a sentence;
    - **Recent runs**;
    - **Keep it running**: the command, with a **Copy** button.
- **If something goes wrong:**
    - *Not running*: no worker waits for events, so nothing starts on its own. Start the command under **Keep it
      running** and leave it open.
    - A run stays waiting: answer it here or on Approvals.
    - *Run only one of awa serve and awa worker per project folder*: the second one refuses to start.

![The Use it page, the form Add a trigger: the kind file-drop, the folder inbox, the pattern *.pdf, the task text and the Add this trigger button](../assets/screenshots/guide/a09-trigger-form.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a09-trigger-form.legend.txt"

![The card of the trigger new-invoice with the sample opened: the name INV-2042.pdf, its text and the button Run it now with this sample](../assets/screenshots/guide/a09-trigger-sample.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a09-trigger-sample.legend.txt"

![Recent runs and Keep it running: the run is done, and the command awa worker blueprint.yaml has a Copy button](../assets/screenshots/guide/a10-use-it-done.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a10-use-it-done.legend.txt"

The trigger that the form writes, and the command that runs it:

```yaml
triggers:
  - name: new-invoice
    file_drop:
      directory: inbox
      pattern: '*.pdf'
    input: 'Check the invoice in {payload.name} and release it for payment. The invoice says: {payload.text}'
```

```console
awa worker blueprint.yaml
```

**Download the project (.zip)** gives your IT team the folder without `.env`, the `.awa` folder or key files. **More
ways to use it (for your IT team)** lists the commands to serve the system as a web API, over MCP or in a terminal.

??? note "The whole window"
    ![The Use it page: Is it running? says Not running, and the run of invoice INV-2042 from the trigger new-invoice waits for your OK](../assets/screenshots/ui-deploy.png)

## Approvals

**Purpose:** answer every run of the project that waits for a person, in one place.

- **You enter:** **Approve** or **Say no** on each card, with a note if you like. **Change the values before approving
  (for experts)** takes new values as a JSON object.
- **In the background:** your answer is saved in the project folder. A running `awa worker` or `awa serve` continues
  the run. When nothing is running, **Continue it now** continues it here.
- **Result:** the run goes on with your decision, or it stops and the agent reads your note.
- **If something goes wrong:**
    - *Nothing waits for you*: no run is paused.
    - *Nothing is running that would continue it*: press **Continue it now**, or start `awa worker` (see
      [Use it](#use-it)).

![The Approvals page: one waiting run from the trigger new-invoice with its card and the buttons Approve and Say no](../assets/screenshots/guide/a10-approvals.png)

--8<-- "docs/assets/screenshots/guide/a10-approvals.legend.txt"

In a terminal: `awa runs list --status waiting`, then `awa runs decide RUN_ID --approve`
([Approvals](approvals.md)).

??? note "The whole window, and on a phone"
    ![The Approvals page: the run of invoice INV-2042 from the trigger new-invoice waits, with its values, Approve and Say no](../assets/screenshots/ui-inbox.png)

    ![The Approvals page on a phone: the waiting run of invoice INV-2042 and the card Please check before this happens](../assets/screenshots/ui-inbox-phone.png)

## Hand the project to a coding assistant

**Purpose:** let a coding assistant extend the project where the draft needs code, such as a tool for your own
system.

The page **Assistant** writes a brief from the project folder. The brief holds:

- the process and the pattern of the agents;
- a map of the files;
- the names of the settings (never their values);
- ready prompts: implement a tool, connect a system, add an MCP server, write more cases;
- templates, and the commands that check the result.

**Copy the brief**, **Download** it or **Save as BRIEF.md**. In a terminal:

```console
awa brief --out BRIEF.md
```

Write a new brief after you change the project. Review what the assistant changed, above all `approvals:` and
`limits:`. Run `awa validate .` and `awa eval . evals/cases.yaml` after every change.

## Is it safe?

- It listens on this computer only. Anything else needs `--allow-remote`, and even then only people with the link
  get in.
- The link carries an access code. The page keeps it in its browser tab and sends it with every request. It is never
  stored in a cookie, so other servers on this computer never see it.
- Every request without the code is refused. Requests from other sites and other host names are refused too. A new
  tab needs the link again.
- With `--allow-remote` the code travels unencrypted over the network: use it only on a network you trust.
- The page loads nothing from the internet and works offline.
- Saved settings go only to `.env` (readable only by you). They are never sent back to the browser and are left out
  of the download.
- Dropped files are checked by their content, kept under safe names and cut off at the size limits. What the AI
  reads of a file is marked as data, not instructions. This lowers the risk of injected instructions, but the
  approvals stay the real barrier.
- Open only projects you trust: a project can contain code (`tools.py`) that runs when awa opens it.

<!-- guide:do cd . -->

!!! example "In code"

    `awa.ui.create_ui_app` returns the same application as a FastAPI app, for example to test it or to serve it with
    your own options; its access code is `app.state.token`:

    <!-- guide:python -->
    ```python
    from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

    from awa.ui import create_ui_app

    app = create_ui_app("invoice-desk")
    with TestClient(app, base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8765") as browser:
        signed_in = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + app.state.token}
        print(browser.get("/api/state").status_code, browser.get("/api/state", headers=signed_in).status_code)
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    401 200
    ```

<!-- source: guide/web-frontend.md -->

# Your own web frontend

Use this page when you build your own web page or app on top of awa. Over plain HTTP, without a client library, your
app uploads files, shows what awa found, builds a process from the files and one sentence, runs it and answers its
approvals. This page is for developers.

The shortest path:

1. [Start the server](#1-start-the-server) with one API key.
2. [Upload files](#2-upload-files) and keep the `upload_id`.
3. [Build a process](#4-build-a-process) from the upload and a sentence, and wait for `completed`.
4. [Run what was built](#6-run-what-was-built) and answer its approvals.

```console
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/uploads -H "Authorization: Bearer $AWA_API_KEY" -F "files=@INV-2041.pdf"
```

You need the server parts of awa (the `[all]` extra and the double-click installer have them). The examples use the
folder `invoice-files` of the [tour](tour.md#step-3-bring-your-files-and-your-ledger). Their output comes from the
page's own test, which runs every step with a scripted model.

!!! info "Preview"
    The HTTP endpoints this page uses work and are tested, but they may still change in a minor release ([Stability](../about/stability.md)).

## How the pieces fit

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    B["Browser<br/>(no key)"] --> Y["Your own backend<br/>(adds the API key)"]
    Y --> S["awa server<br/>uploads, profiles, builds, runs"]
```

Keep the awa API key on your backend, never in the page: whoever opens a page can read it. Your backend forwards the
calls and adds the header `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY`. The browser examples use `fetch`; a browser
`EventSource` cannot send that header.

## 1. Start the server

Create the folder `web-demo` with the file `server.py`. The server takes **one API key** from the environment. The
key belongs to a *principal*: a name, a tenant (each customer's data is kept apart) and roles. `DataOptions(root=...)`
is the folder for uploads and builds, one subfolder per tenant:

<!-- guide:do cd . -->
<!-- guide:file web-demo/server.py -->
```python
import os

from awa.server import ApiKeyAuthenticator, DataOptions, Principal, create_app

auth = ApiKeyAuthenticator(
    {os.environ["AWA_API_KEY"]: Principal("web-app", tenant="acme", roles={"builder"})}
)
app = create_app(
    [],  # no process to serve yet: this server only takes files and builds
    authenticator=auth,
    data=DataOptions(root="awa-data", roles={"builder"}),
)
```

<!-- guide:do cd web-demo -->

`create_app([])` serves no ready-made process: this server takes files and builds. Without `root`, awa keeps everything in memory and says so in its log. That is fine for a try-out, but everything is
gone when the server stops.

=== "Start it"

    ```console
    $ export AWA_API_KEY=pick-a-long-random-secret
    $ uvicorn server:app --port 8000
    ```

    On Windows PowerShell use `$env:AWA_API_KEY = "pick-a-long-random-secret"`. Check that it runs:

    ```console
    $ curl -s localhost:8000/v1/health
    {"status":"ok"}
    ```

=== "Run it here"

    The next scripts need no server. This helper runs the same `app` inside the Python process on its own thread, so a
    build runs only while the script that started it is alive. It offers `get` and `post` like a web client and keeps
    the ids between scripts in a file. Save it next to `server.py`:

    <!-- guide:python save=client.py -->
    ```python
    import asyncio
    import json
    import os
    import threading
    import time
    from pathlib import Path

    import httpx

    KEY = os.environ.setdefault("AWA_API_KEY", "pick-a-long-random-secret")
    from server import app  # noqa: E402

    loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()  # the app and its builds live on this loop
    threading.Thread(target=loop.run_forever, daemon=True).start()
    client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        transport=httpx.ASGITransport(app=app),
        base_url="http://localhost:8000",
        headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + KEY},
    )
    STATE = Path("state.json")

    def request(method, path, **kwargs):
        return asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(client.request(method, path, **kwargs), loop).result(60)

    def get(path, **kwargs):
        return request("GET", path, **kwargs)

    def post(path, **kwargs):
        return request("POST", path, **kwargs)

    def remember(**ids):
        state = json.loads(STATE.read_text()) if STATE.exists() else {}
        STATE.write_text(json.dumps({**state, **ids}))

    def recall(name):
        return json.loads(STATE.read_text())[name]

    def show(response):
        print(response.status_code, json.dumps(response.json(), indent=2))

    def wait(build_id, until=("completed", "failed", "needs_input")):
        while True:
            state = get(f"/v1/builds/{build_id}").json()
            if state["status"] in until:
                return state
            time.sleep(0.1)
    ```

## 2. Upload files

Send the files as a multipart form with the field name `files`, one part per file. Every part with a file name counts as a file; with `curl`, repeat `-F` for several files. The answer holds an `upload_id`;
every next step uses it.

=== "curl"

    ```console
    $ curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/uploads \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $AWA_API_KEY" \
        -F "files=@INV-2041.pdf" -F "files=@INV-2042.pdf" -F "files=@purchase_orders.csv"
    ```

=== "Python"

    <!-- guide:python -->
    ```python
    from pathlib import Path

    from client import post, remember, show

    files = [
        ("files", (path.name, path.read_bytes(), "application/octet-stream"))
        for path in sorted(Path("../invoice-files").iterdir())
    ]
    answer = post("/v1/uploads", files=files)
    remember(upload_id=answer.json()["upload_id"])
    show(answer)
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    201 {
      "upload_id": "up_3dd77b1f913f416ebfc4e29c",
      "files": [
        {
          "id": "f1",
          "name": "INV-2041.pdf",
          "size": 813,
          "kind": "pdf",
          "sniffed_type": "application/pdf",
          "sha256": "bd6d6f7a1ca9ed6d231b80c7e3a0e307ac4c1e099b2602e843d4cd381650fbd4",
          "status": "ok"
        },
        {
          "id": "f2",
          "name": "INV-2042.pdf",
          "size": 823,
          "kind": "pdf",
          "sniffed_type": "application/pdf",
          "sha256": "f3cfd7a7a0af1e05c5eb35ff7989126cfcd9b5598e7ac3807f911ea485adb1ac",
          "status": "ok"
        },
        {
          "id": "f3",
          "name": "purchase_orders.csv",
          "size": 109,
          "kind": "csv",
          "sniffed_type": "text/csv",
          "sha256": "607297b567461bcb3fcbe525e721a174c954e4e3727426343fc70f6ac902d14d",
          "status": "ok"
        }
      ],
      "total_bytes": 1745,
      "created_at": "2026-10-06T05:40:13.114084+00:00",
      "expires_at": "2026-10-07T05:40:13.114084+00:00"
    }
    ```

What awa checks before it keeps a file:

- **The content decides the type**, not the name and not what the browser says. A `.pdf` that is not a PDF is refused
  with `415` and the code `awa.data.type_mismatch`. Accepted: CSV, Excel, PDF, Word, email (`.eml`, `.mbox`), JSON, SQLite,
  text, and zip files of those.
- **File names are cleaned.** No folders, no `..`, no reserved names. awa chooses where a file is stored.
- **Zip files are opened only after every entry was checked.** A zip that unpacks into far more than it claims, or an
  entry that wants to leave its folder, is refused (`422`, `awa.data.zip_unsafe`).
- **Size.** 25 MB for a file and 100 MB for an upload by default, stopped while the file is still arriving (`413`).

The files are kept for 24 hours (`expires_at`); `DELETE /v1/uploads/{upload_id}` removes them sooner. To make a
retry safe, send the header `Idempotency-Key: ANY-UNIQUE-TEXT`. A repeated request then gets the first answer and the
header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and the files are not stored twice.

In the browser, use `fetch`. Do not set `Content-Type` yourself: the browser adds it with the boundary awa needs:

```js
const API = "/awa"; // your backend, which forwards to awa and adds the key

async function problem(response) {
  const { error } = await response.json();
  return new Error(`${error.code}: ${error.message}`);
}

async function upload(files) {
  const body = new FormData();
  for (const file of files) body.append("files", file); // one part for each file
  const response = await fetch(`${API}/v1/uploads`, { method: "POST", body });
  if (!response.ok) throw await problem(response);
  return response.json();
}
```

## 3. Show what awa found

`POST /v1/data/profile` returns what is in the files: each file's kind, tables and columns, the number and date
formats (`4.250,00` is a decimal with a comma), and flags for problems such as a scan without text or a row of
totals. An unreadable file gets a flag, not an HTTP error. No model is called and the files are not changed.

=== "curl"

    ```console
    $ curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/data/profile \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $AWA_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d '{"upload_id": "UPLOAD_ID"}'
    ```

=== "Python"

    <!-- guide:python -->
    ```python
    from client import post, recall

    answer = post("/v1/data/profile", json={"upload_id": recall("upload_id")})
    body = answer.json()
    print(answer.status_code, sorted(body))
    print(body["profile"]["summary"])
    for file in body["profile"]["files"]:
        print(file["path"], file["kind"], file["status"])
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    200 ['profile', 'upload_id']
    {'files': 3, 'tables': 1, 'rows': 2, 'warnings': 0, 'errors': 0}
    INV-2041.pdf pdf ok
    INV-2042.pdf pdf ok
    purchase_orders.csv csv ok
    ```

The shape of `profile` is the JSON Schema `src/awa/data/profile.v1.schema.json` in the awa folder. Useful extras:

- `"mask": "drop"` leaves every sample value out.
- `"files": ["f1"]` profiles only some files.
- `"budget_tokens": 3000` (or any `mask`) adds `model_view`: the short text a model would see instead of your data,
  with personal data replaced when `mask` is `placeholders`.

## 4. Build a process

Send a sentence or two about what should happen and the `upload_id`. A note for one file is optional
(`"notes": [{"file": "purchase_orders.csv", "text": "..."}]`). The build runs in the background: it reads the files,
writes tests from the real rows, designs the process and runs the tests on a copy. Your files are never changed. It
usually takes a few minutes and uses model calls. `options` limit it (`rounds`, `target`, `max_requests`, `model`,
`mask`, `guidance`), and the server caps them.

=== "curl"

    ```console
    $ curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/builds \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $AWA_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d '{"description": "Check each invoice against the open purchase orders.", "upload_id": "UPLOAD_ID"}'
    ```

=== "Python"

    <!-- guide:python model=files -->
    ```python
    from client import post, recall, remember, show, wait

    DESCRIPTION = (
        "Supplier invoices arrive as PDF files. Check each invoice against the open purchase orders "
        "in purchase_orders.csv: the purchase order must be open and the amount must match. A "
        "matching invoice is released for payment. From 5,000 EUR the head of finance must approve "
        "the payment first."
    )
    started = post(
        "/v1/builds",
        json={
            "description": DESCRIPTION,
            "upload_id": recall("upload_id"),
            "notes": [{"file": "purchase_orders.csv", "text": "Look up by PO number."}],
        },
    )
    remember(build_id=started.json()["build_id"])
    show(started)
    print(wait(started.json()["build_id"])["status"])  # keeps this script alive until the build is over
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    202 {
      "build_id": "bld_9e13a2bcf7664dd088ce3eec",
      "status": "queued",
      "events_url": "/v1/builds/bld_9e13a2bcf7664dd088ce3eec/events",
      "url": "/v1/builds/bld_9e13a2bcf7664dd088ce3eec"
    }
    completed
    ```

`202` means the build was accepted and runs on its own. Poll its state or follow its events.

### Follow the progress

`GET /v1/builds/{build_id}` returns the `status`: `queued`, `profiling`, `designing`, `evaluating`, `repairing`,
`writing`, `needs_input`, `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`. It also returns the round, the pass rate and the model
use so far, and at the end the `report` or the `error`.

=== "curl"

    ```console
    $ curl -s localhost:8000/v1/builds/BUILD_ID -H "Authorization: Bearer $AWA_API_KEY"
    ```

=== "Python"

    <!-- guide:python -->
    ```python
    from client import recall, wait

    state = wait(recall("build_id"))
    report = state["report"]
    print(state["status"], state["stage"], state["round"], state["pass_rate"])
    print(report["summary"])
    print(report["passed"], report["rounds"], report["stopped"], report["flaky"], report["failing"])
    print(report["files"])
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    completed write 1 1.0
    invoice_check: 2 of 2 eval cases pass (100%) on the local workspace after 1 round(s); target reached.
    True 1 target_reached [] []
    ['.env.example', '.gitignore', 'CONNECT.md', 'README.md', 'blueprint.yaml', 'data/PROFILE.json', 'data/PROFILE.md', 'data/files/INV-2041.pdf', 'data/files/INV-2042.pdf', 'data/files/purchase_orders.csv', 'evals/cases.yaml', 'tests/test_tools.py', 'tools.py']
    ```

Instead of polling, follow the build as a stream of Server-Sent Events. Each event has a number (`id`). If the
connection drops, ask again with `Last-Event-ID: LAST-NUMBER-YOU-GOT` to get only what you missed. A finished build
answers `204` once everything was sent. Closing the stream does not stop the build.

=== "curl"

    ```console
    $ curl -s -N localhost:8000/v1/builds/BUILD_ID/events -H "Authorization: Bearer $AWA_API_KEY"
    ```

=== "Python"

    <!-- guide:python -->
    ```python
    import json

    from client import get, recall

    events = get(f"/v1/builds/{recall('build_id')}/events")
    frames = [frame for frame in events.text.split("\n\n") if frame.strip()]
    print(events.status_code, len(frames), "events")
    print([frame.splitlines()[1].removeprefix("event: ") for frame in frames])
    first = frames[0].splitlines()
    print(first[0])
    print(first[1])
    print(json.dumps(json.loads(first[2].removeprefix("data: ")), indent=2))
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    200 15 events
    ['build.started', 'data.profile.file', 'data.profile.file', 'data.profile.file', 'data.profile.done', 'build.progress', 'design.acceptance', 'design.architecture', 'eval.round.started', 'eval.case', 'eval.case', 'eval.round.finished', 'build.progress', 'write.done', 'build.completed']
    id: 1
    event: build.started
    {
      "seq": 1,
      "ts": "2026-10-06T05:40:14.060536+00:00",
      "type": "build.started",
      "build_id": "bld_9e13a2bcf7664dd088ce3eec",
      "data": {
        "stage": "profile",
        "upload_id": "up_3dd77b1f913f416ebfc4e29c",
        "answers": 0
      }
    }
    ```

What the event types mean:

| Event | When |
| --- | --- |
| `build.started` | The build begins. |
| `data.profile.file`, `data.profile.done` | A file was read, then all of them. |
| `design.acceptance`, `design.validation`, `design.architecture` | The tests are written and checked, the design is made. |
| `eval.round.started`, `eval.case`, `eval.round.finished` | A test round runs, case by case, with its pass rate. |
| `eval.round.stopped` | The model-call limit ended a round early; the best earlier round is kept. |
| `repair.started` | A round failed and the design is repaired. |
| `write.done` | The project folder is written. |
| `build.progress` | Any other step of the build: its stage, round, message and the pass rate so far. |
| `build.question` | awa needs your answer (below). |
| `build.completed`, `build.failed`, `build.cancelled` | Exactly one of them ends the build. |

In the browser, use `fetch`. `follow` calls `onEvent` for every event and returns the number of the last one, so a
lost connection can continue where it stopped:

```js
async function post(path, json) {
  const response = await fetch(`${API}${path}`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify(json),
  });
  if (!response.ok) throw await problem(response);
  return response.json();
}

async function follow(buildId, onEvent, lastId = 0) {
  const response = await fetch(`${API}/v1/builds/${buildId}/events`, {
    headers: { "Last-Event-ID": String(lastId) },
  });
  if (response.status === 204) return lastId; // over, and everything was sent
  const reader = response.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader();
  let buffer = "";
  for (;;) {
    const { value, done } = await reader.read();
    if (done) return lastId;
    buffer += value;
    let end;
    while ((end = buffer.indexOf("\n\n")) >= 0) {
      const frame = buffer.slice(0, end);
      buffer = buffer.slice(end + 2);
      const data = frame.split("\n").find((line) => line.startsWith("data: "));
      if (!data) continue;
      const event = JSON.parse(data.slice(6));
      lastId = event.seq;
      onEvent(event);
      const last = ["build.completed", "build.failed", "build.cancelled", "build.question"];
      if (last.includes(event.type)) return lastId;
    }
  }
}
```

### When awa has a question

If the sentence does not fit the files (CV screening, but the files are invoices), awa does not guess. The build
stops with the status `needs_input` and a list of `questions`; `evidence` names the parts of the profile each one is
about. Show the question to your user and send the answer with `POST /v1/builds/{id}/answers`, and the build goes on.
awa never takes an answer from a file's content, so a file cannot answer for the user.

=== "curl"

    ```console
    $ curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/builds/BUILD_ID/answers \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $AWA_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d '{"answers": [{"id": "q1", "value": "Use purchase_orders.csv for the invoices."}]}'
    ```

=== "Python"

    <!-- guide:python model=files -->
    ```python
    import json
    from pathlib import Path

    from client import get, post, wait

    files = [
        ("files", (path.name, path.read_bytes(), "application/octet-stream"))
        for path in sorted(Path("../invoice-files").iterdir())
    ]
    upload = post("/v1/uploads", files=files).json()["upload_id"]
    started = post(
        "/v1/builds",
        json={
            "description": "Screen the incoming CVs against our role profile and schedule interviews.",
            "upload_id": upload,
        },
    )
    build_id = started.json()["build_id"]
    waiting = wait(build_id)
    print(waiting["status"])
    print(json.dumps(waiting["questions"], indent=2))
    answer = {"answers": [{"id": "q1", "value": "Use purchase_orders.csv for the invoices."}]}
    accepted = post(f"/v1/builds/{build_id}/answers", json=answer)
    print(accepted.status_code)
    done = wait(build_id, until=("completed", "failed"))
    print(done["status"], done["pass_rate"])
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    needs_input
    [
      {
        "id": "q1",
        "text": "The description is about CVs or candidates, but the files hold purchase_orders.csv (po, vendor, amount, status). Which file is it, or should other files be added?",
        "options": [],
        "evidence": [
          "f3.t1.po",
          "f3.t1.vendor"
        ]
      }
    ]
    202
    completed 1.0
    ```

The command-line build asks the same questions and takes the same answers ([Your files](files.md#when-the-words-do-not-fit-the-files)).

### Stop a build

`DELETE /v1/builds/{build_id}` stops it. Stopping a finished build changes nothing.

## 5. Read the result

When the status is `completed`, `report` says what happened:

- `passed`: whether the tests reached the target.
- `failing`: the tests that did not pass; `flaky`: those that passed only on a second try. Look at both.
- `assumptions`: what awa had to assume.

Two calls give you the project itself:

- `GET /v1/builds/{build_id}/files/README.md` shows one text file of the project (also `blueprint.yaml`,
  `evals/cases.yaml` and `data/PROFILE.json`).
- `GET /v1/builds/{build_id}/project.zip` downloads the whole project. Settings files with secrets are never
  included.

A `failed` build names the reason in `error.code`:

- `awa.build.usage_limit`: the model calls ran out. Raise `max_requests`.
- `awa.build.design_invalid`: no valid design could be made. `error.details.issues` says what was wrong, or why the
  files cannot be used.

=== "curl"

    ```console
    $ curl -s localhost:8000/v1/builds/BUILD_ID/files/README.md -H "Authorization: Bearer $AWA_API_KEY"
    $ curl -s -o project.zip localhost:8000/v1/builds/BUILD_ID/project.zip -H "Authorization: Bearer $AWA_API_KEY"
    ```

=== "Python"

    <!-- guide:python -->
    ```python
    import io
    import zipfile

    from client import get, recall

    build = f"/v1/builds/{recall('build_id')}"
    readme = get(build + "/files/README.md")
    print(readme.status_code, readme.text.splitlines()[0])
    archive = get(build + "/project.zip")
    print(archive.status_code, archive.headers["content-type"])
    print(sorted(zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(archive.content)).namelist()))
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    200 # invoice_check
    200 application/zip
    ['.env.example', '.gitignore', 'CONNECT.md', 'README.md', 'blueprint.yaml', 'data/PROFILE.json', 'data/PROFILE.md', 'data/files/INV-2041.pdf', 'data/files/INV-2042.pdf', 'data/files/purchase_orders.csv', 'evals/cases.yaml', 'tests/test_tools.py', 'tools.py']
    ```

## 6. Run what was built

`POST /v1/builds/{build_id}/runs` runs the built process. It answers with `text`, `status`, `thread_id` and `usage`.
Add `"file": "f1"` to process one file, `?mode=async` to get the answer later, or `?stream=true` to watch.

When the process needs an approval (a payment, a write), the answer has `"status": "interrupted"`:

1. Read what it wants with `GET .../threads/{thread_id}/interrupts`.
2. Answer with `POST .../threads/{thread_id}/resume`.

The large invoice needs two approvals: the head of finance first, then writing the result:

=== "curl"

    ```console
    $ curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/builds/BUILD_ID/runs \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $AWA_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d '{"input": "Check the invoice in INV-2042.pdf and release it for payment."}'
    $ curl -s localhost:8000/v1/builds/BUILD_ID/threads/THREAD_ID/interrupts \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $AWA_API_KEY"
    $ curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/builds/BUILD_ID/threads/THREAD_ID/resume \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $AWA_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d '{"decision": {"action": "approve"}}'
    ```

=== "Python"

    <!-- guide:python model=files -->
    ```python
    from client import get, post, recall

    build = f"/v1/builds/{recall('build_id')}"
    run = post(
        build + "/runs", json={"input": "Check the invoice in INV-2042.pdf and release it for payment."}
    ).json()
    thread = build + f"/threads/{run['thread_id']}"
    while run["status"] == "interrupted":
        asked = get(thread + "/interrupts").json()["interrupts"][0]["value"]
        print("waiting for approval of", asked["tool"], asked["args"])
        run = post(thread + "/resume", json={"decision": {"action": "approve"}}).json()
    print(run["status"], run["text"])
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    Approvals of runs of invoice_check are kept in memory and are lost when the server restarts
    waiting for approval of finance_approval {'po': 'PO-7725', 'amount_eur': 7450.0}
    waiting for approval of output_write_file {'path': 'INV-2042.txt', 'content': 'INV-2042: purchase order PO-7725 is open and the amount 7,450.00 EUR matches.', 'overwrite': False}
    completed INV-2042: purchase order PO-7725 matches 7,450.00 EUR; released for payment.
    ```

`DataOptions(approver_roles={"approver"})` lets only callers with that role approve. Approvals of these runs live in
the server's memory and are lost when it restarts.

## What the limits are

| What happens | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| A file or an upload is too large | `413`, `awa.data.too_large` |
| More files than allowed (200) | `413`, `awa.data.too_many_files` |
| Wrong or lying file type | `415`, `awa.data.unsupported_type` or `awa.data.type_mismatch` |
| The client is too slow (30 s without data) | `408`, `awa.data.upload_timeout` |
| Your tenant stores too much (1 GB), receives too many uploads at once, or runs too many builds | `429`, `awa.data.quota_exceeded` (see `Retry-After`) |
| Too many requests | `429`, `awa.rate_limit_exceeded` |
| An id that does not exist, or belongs to someone else | `404`, the same answer for both, on purpose |

## Good to know

- **Everything is kept for one tenant.** Another tenant cannot see, guess or run your builds.
- **The server never shows where it keeps files** on its disk.
- **After a restart:** a build that was running is `failed`. Finished builds, builds that wait for answers and their uploads
  survive. Uploads are removed after 24 hours, finished builds after 7 days.
- **awa does not scan files for viruses.** If you need that, give `DataOptions(scanner=...)` a scanner.
- **Text inside files can try to give orders to the model** ("ignore your rules ..."). awa marks such text as data, flags
  it in the profile and keeps the approvals of the built process on. This lowers the risk. It is not a guarantee: keep
  approvals on for anything that changes things.
- **The contract.** The file `docs/develop/data-api.openapi.json` in the awa folder describes every endpoint for tools that
  generate clients. [Serving](../develop/serving.md) lists them with the authentication and the limits.

## Common mistakes

| You see | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `401` | The `Authorization: Bearer` header is missing or the key is wrong; check it on your backend. |
| `403` | The principal has no role that `DataOptions(roles=...)` allows. |
| `415` for a good file | The content is not what the ending says; open the file yourself. |
| `409` on `answers` | The build does not wait for an answer; read its status first. |
| A build stays `queued` | The server runs at most two builds at once for a tenant; `GET /v1/builds` lists them. |
| The page cannot read the events | Use `fetch` through your backend, not `EventSource`: it cannot send the key. |

!!! example "In code"

    Every error has the same shape: show the `message` to your user and log the `request_id`.

    <!-- guide:python -->
    ```python
    from client import get, post

    fake = [("files", ("invoice.pdf", b"this is not a pdf", "application/pdf"))]
    refused = post("/v1/uploads", files=fake)
    print(refused.status_code, refused.json()["error"]["code"])
    print(sorted(refused.json()["error"]))
    unknown = get("/v1/builds/bld_does_not_exist")
    print(unknown.status_code, unknown.json()["error"]["code"])
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    415 awa.data.type_mismatch
    ['code', 'message', 'request_id', 'retryable', 'type']
    404 awa.build.not_found
    ```

<!-- source: guide/examples.md -->

# Examples

The examples are small, finished processes you can copy. Each one already has its approvals, limits and eval cases.
Copy the folder closest to your process, run it on its sample data, then adapt it.

## Try an example

The examples are in the awa folder under `examples/`; a wheel does not contain them. Copy a folder to your work
folder and open a terminal in it. `awa validate` checks it and `awa show` describes it; neither needs a model:

<!-- guide:do cd . -->
<!-- guide:do copy awa:examples/recipes/invoice-processing invoice-processing -->
<!-- guide:do cd invoice-processing -->
<!-- guide:run -->
```console
$ awa validate blueprint.yaml
invoice-processing: valid
$ awa show blueprint.yaml
invoice-processing 1.0.0
Extracts, validates, policy-checks and books incoming supplier invoices.
entrypoint: team

agent           model    tools                                              skills                                  description
ap_coordinator  default  book_invoice, hold_invoice, notify_vendor          delegation-briefs, approval-requests    Runs each invoice through extraction, validation and the ...
extractor       default  fetch_invoice_document                             document-extraction, structured-output  Reads an invoice document and extracts its fields exactly...
validator       default  get_vendor, get_purchase_order, get_goods_receipt  data-validation                         Matches invoice fields against the vendor master, purchas...
policy_checker  default  get_ap_policy, get_vendor, find_booked_invoices    policy-compliance-check                 Checks an invoice against the AP policy (duplicates, bank...

team invoice-processing: orchestrator ap_coordinator
  delegates: ap_coordinator -> extractor, validator, policy_checker
  shared: none

approvals: book_invoice (when tools:booking_needs_approval), notify_vendor (when tools:vendor_note_needs_approval)
```

With a model key you can go further:

- `awa run blueprint.yaml "Process invoice document DOC-1002." --stream` runs the recipe on its sample systems. It
  stops before it books the invoice above 10,000 EUR.
- `awa eval blueprint.yaml cases.yaml` runs its eval cases.

In the web app, **Start from an example** on the page **Data** opens an example as a new project. From a terminal,
`awa ui --example ID` does the same.

!!! note "What the release checks prove"

    Every example is checked offline on scripted models with every release. The blueprint is valid, a realistic case
    runs from start to end including the pause for approval, and every eval case passes. That proves the flow, not
    the quality of a real model's answers. Measure that with `awa eval blueprint.yaml cases.yaml --repetitions 3`
    before you rely on an example.

## Recipes

Recipes are multi-agent starting points in `examples/recipes/`. Their tools work on small built-in sample systems.
Each tool's description says what it does against the external system.

| Recipe | Process | Structure | Waits for a person |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invoice-processing` | Read the invoice, match it with order and receipt, check the AP policy, book or hold, tell the vendor | Team | Booking above 10,000 EUR; free-text messages to vendors |
| `customer-support-desk` | Triage, billing, technical and returns agents, refunds, escalation | Team with handoffs | Refunds above 50.00 |
| `lead-qualification` | Research, fit score, CRM update, first email | Team | Every email |
| `employee-onboarding` | Accounts, hardware, payroll, buddy, desk, badge, first-week plan | Network on a task board | In the systems of record |
| `contract-review` | Legal, compliance and commercial review, verdict with proposed changes | Workflow, reviews side by side | None (advice only) |
| `it-incident-triage` | Severity, paging, diagnosis from the runbook, status updates, notes afterwards | Team | Paging for the most severe incidents; public status updates |
| `market-research-report` | Research in parallel, analysis, sourced report, review loop | Network on a task board | None (internal report) |
| `content-production` | Brief, draft and edit until approved, compliance check, publication | Workflow with a loop | Every publication |
| `deep-research` | Plan, parallel web researchers, a citation agent that checks every quote, saved report | Team with a shared blackboard | Saving the report |

## Use case examples

Use cases in `examples/usecases/` are typical company processes that end in an action. They are small first tests on
sample data, and they show that the library applies to many kinds of processes. In each folder:

- connectors read the files and systems;
- `tools.py` holds only the rules, calculations and writes a model must not improvise;
- `make_data.py` writes the sample data again whenever you run it.

| Use case | Process | Waits for a person | Trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `purchase-requisition` | Requisition email, approved supplier, budget check, purchase order, order email | Orders above 1,000 EUR; every supplier email | no |
| `expense-report-audit` | Report lines and receipt PDFs against the travel policy, flags, reimbursement | Reports above 500 EUR or with a serious flag | no |
| `supplier-due-diligence` | Sanctions, adverse news and ownership checked on the web with cited sources | Every recorded decision | no |
| `order-to-cash-exceptions` | Orders (SQLite), invoices (Excel) and payments (CSV) compared, mismatches classified, dunning letters | Every dunning letter | no |
| `recruiting-cv-screening` | PDF and Word CVs to structured profiles, explainable score, shortlist, interview invitations | Every invitation | no |
| `meeting-notes-to-tasks` | Notes to decisions, owned tasks with due dates on the board, follow-up email | Every follow-up email | no |
| `compliance-news-watch` | Web search per topic, change detection against the previous digest, digest email with sources | Every digest email | schedule |
| `data-quality-reconciliation` | An Excel export dropped in a folder compared with a SQL table, update proposals | Every database change | file drop |
| `email-inbox-triage` | Classify mail, look up the sender, route to a team's task board, draft replies | Every outgoing reply | mailbox |
| `weekly-management-report` | KPIs from SQL against the prior week and the budget, variance explanations, summary email | The management email | schedule |
| `inventory-replenishment` | Stock over REST, demand from SQL, reorder rule, purchase orders in the ERP | Purchase orders above 5,000 EUR | schedule and webhook |
| `incident-postmortem` | Timeline from logs, tickets and deployments, blameless postmortem draft | Publishing the postmortem | webhook |
| `sales-operations` | Sales questions answered with SQL on 6,000 generated orders; expected answers computed from the data | Discounts above 10 percent | no |

The data of every use case is test data, public or generated; each `data/ORIGIN.md` names where it comes from. For
the processes on Microsoft 365 mail and files, see [Microsoft 365](microsoft-365.md).

## Adapt an example

1. **Copy the folder** and give the process its own `name:` in `blueprint.yaml`.
2. **Rewrite the instructions** for your process: your categories, formats and escalation paths.
3. **Connect your systems** one at a time. Use a [connector](connect.md) in the agents' `tools`. Or let a developer
   replace the body of a tool in `tools.py` and keep its name, inputs and description: the agents and the eval cases
   rely on them.
4. **Keep every approval.** Each one guards an action that cannot be undone or that leaves the company. Tighten a
   condition rather than removing it.
5. **Keep the rules in code.** Thresholds live in `tools.py` and in the approval conditions, never only in the
   instructions. `when: tools:booking_needs_approval` names a function in `tools.py`.
6. **Size the limits** to your volumes.
7. **Add your own eval cases**, above all the exceptions that go wrong today ([Test and improve](test.md)).

Requisitions, receipts, CVs, emails and web pages come from outside the process. Every example frames them as data,
and its `cases.yaml` has at least one document that tries to give the agent orders.

!!! example "In code"

    An example is a blueprint like any other, readable from Python ([Blueprints](../develop/blueprints.md)):

    <!-- guide:python -->
    ```python
    from awa.blueprints import Blueprint

    recipe = Blueprint.from_yaml_file("blueprint.yaml")
    print(recipe.team.orchestrator, [approval.tool for approval in recipe.approvals])
    ```

    <!-- guide:expect -->
    ```text
    ap_coordinator ['book_invoice', 'notify_vendor']
    ```

<!-- source: guide/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

Use this page when something does not work. Find the message you see, then apply the fix next to it.

When you do not know where to start, go in this order:

1. Run `awa doctor`. It checks your setup. Do the `fix:` line under every `FAIL` or `WARN`.
2. When every line says `OK`, run `awa validate blueprint.yaml`. If it prints `error:`, fix the line it names.
3. When the blueprint is valid, run the process, then read what it did with `awa runs trace RUN`
   ([Keep it running](operate.md#read-a-trace)).

A few things help with every message:

- Run commands in the project folder, the one with `blueprint.yaml` and `.env`.
- Every error starts with `error:` and ends with what to do. Read it to its end.
- `awa --verbose` before a command prints the technical details for your IT team.
- The messages below are copied from awa. Your operating system words its own messages in your language.

## What `awa doctor` tells you

| Line | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OK` | The check passed. | Nothing. |
| `INFO` | A fact, nothing is wrong. | Read it when something else fails. |
| `WARN` | Something you need for real runs is missing, such as a key. | Do the `fix:` line under it. |
| `FAIL` | Something blocks use: an old Python, a missing package, settings that do not validate. | Do the `fix:` line; the result is `NOT usable`. |

The last line says `Result: usable`, with warnings, or `NOT usable`. The exit code is 0, 78 (a required part is
missing) or 1.

## Setup and keys

| You see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `'awa' is not recognized` | The terminal does not know where awa is | See [`awa` is not found](#awa-is-not-found). |
| `credentials ABSENT`, or an authentication error | No key in the folder you work in | See [There is no model key](#there-is-no-model-key). |
| `Cannot create chat model`, or a model not found | The model name is wrong | See [The model name is wrong](#the-model-name-is-wrong). |
| The browser says *Open the link from the awa window* | The link carries a one-time code | Copy the link that `awa ui` printed into the address bar. |
| `error while attempting to bind on address` (`address already in use`) | Another program uses the port | `awa serve ... --port 8001`, or stop the other program. `awa ui` picks a free port by itself. |
| `PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied` | A protected folder such as `C:\Windows` | Work in your own folders, with short paths; quote paths with spaces. |
| `unrecognized arguments` | A text with spaces is not in quotes | See [Quotes around the text](#quotes-around-the-text). |

### There is no model key

```text
WARN  credentials:anthropic  credentials ABSENT (profiles default, fast, strong); real model calls will fail, offline tests still work
                             fix: set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env or the environment
```

Every run calls an AI model, and the provider needs your key.

- **In the web app:** open **Set up** and paste the key.
- **In a terminal:** put one line `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...` (the setting of your provider) into `.env` in the project
  folder. awa reads `.env` only from the folder you run it in. `awa doctor` says `no .env in <folder>` when it is
  not there.

Without a key, `awa validate`, `awa show` and the offline tests of a project still work.

### The model name is wrong

```text
error: Cannot create chat model 'anthropc:<model>': Unable to infer model provider for model='anthropc:<model>'. ...
```

A model is written `provider:model-name`. Copy the model name from your provider's list. Set it as
`AWA_DEFAULT_MODEL` in `.env`, or on **Set up**. `awa doctor` prints the default model it will use. A provider that
does not know the model answers `HTTP 404, model not found`.

### `awa` is not found

The command lives in the environment the install created.

- **After the double-click installer:** use the **awa** shortcut, or run the `PATH` line the installer printed, once
  per terminal window.
- **After a manual install:** activate the environment (`.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` in PowerShell), or call
  `python -m awa`.
- **PowerShell says that running scripts is disabled:** run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned`
  once.

[Install](../start/install.md) has the details.

### Quotes around the text

```text
awa: error: unrecognized arguments: is order 1001
```

The shell splits text at spaces. Put the whole text in double quotes: `awa run blueprint.yaml "Where is order 1001?"`.

Windows PowerShell 5.1 removes double quotes inside an argument. So put JSON values (`--args`, `--payload`,
`--edit-args`, `--deps`) into a file and give it as `"@file.json"`; that works in every shell. A long description is
