### `awa export`

```text
usage: awa export [-h] [--out DIR] [--check] [--force] [--json] [project]

Write a standalone LangChain and LangGraph project from a blueprint with one agent. It runs
without awa and is edited with LangChain and LangGraph only; nothing syncs back. A blueprint that
uses anything the export does not carry over is refused as a whole.

positional arguments:
  project     project folder or blueprint file (default .)

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --out DIR   folder to write; must not exist yet
  --check     render and import the project in a temporary folder; write nothing
  --force     replace an earlier export in --out (never other files)
  --json      print the result as JSON
```

## Check

### `awa validate`

```text
usage: awa validate [-h] [--tools FILES] [--skills DIR] [--profile {authored,generated}] [--notes]
                    blueprint

Check a blueprint for errors without running it or calling a model: the schema, the agents, the
tool names (with the tools.py beside it) and the triggers. Exit code 0 when it is valid (warnings
are printed), 1 on errors.

positional arguments:
  blueprint             blueprint file (YAML or JSON) or project folder

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --tools FILES         more tool files or modules, comma-separated (repeatable); the tools.py
                        next to the blueprint is always loaded
  --skills DIR          more skill folders (repeatable); skills/ next to the blueprint is always
                        loaded
  --profile {authored,generated}
                        lint profile: authored (default) or generated (every rule strict)
  --notes               also print every lint note
```

### `awa show`

```text
usage: awa show [-h] [--tools FILES] [--skills DIR] [--mermaid] [--input VALUES]
                [--fail STEP[=TRIES]] [--decide {approve,reject}]
                [{cases,dry-run}] blueprint

Describe a blueprint: its agents, models, tools, skills, triggers, approvals and how the agents
work together. `show cases` lists the special cases and their tests, `show dry-run` walks the path
a run would take; neither calls a model.

positional arguments:
  {cases,dry-run}       cases: the special cases in words and their boundary tests; dry-run: the
                        path a run would take with --input values; both without a model
  blueprint             blueprint file (YAML or JSON) or project folder

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --tools FILES         more tool files or modules, comma-separated (repeatable); the tools.py
                        next to the blueprint is always loaded
  --skills DIR          more skill folders (repeatable); skills/ next to the blueprint is always
                        loaded
  --mermaid             print a Mermaid diagram only
  --input VALUES        dry-run: the field values the steps answer, as a JSON object or a
                        .json/.yaml file; {"<step>": {...}} gives one step its own values
  --fail STEP[=TRIES]   dry-run: let the first TRIES tries of STEP fail with an error (default 1)
  --decide {approve,reject}
                        dry-run: how every question to a person is answered (default approve)
```

### `awa eval`

```text
usage: awa eval [-h] [--tools FILES] [--skills DIR] [--agent NAME] [--scorer SPEC] [--tag TAG]
                [--case ID] [--concurrency N] [--repetitions N] [--timeout SECONDS]
                [--max-requests N] [--max-total-tokens N] [--max-tool-calls N] [--max-cost AMOUNT]
                [--max-duration TIME] [--sandbox DIR] [--no-sandbox] [--judge-model MODEL]
                [--fail-fast] [--json FILE] [--markdown FILE] [--format {text,markdown}]
                [--baseline FILE] [--min-pass-rate RATE] [--min-pass-hat-k R]
                [--cost-budget AMOUNT] [--prices FILE] [--tolerance DROP] [--replay]
                [--replay-store FILE] [--search-fixture FILE] [--record-search] [--deps JSON]
                [--user-id ID]
                blueprint dataset

Run every case of a dataset (evals/cases.yaml) against the system and print the pass rate as a
table. Needs a model key (awa setup sets it, awa doctor checks it). Exit code 1 below --min-pass-
rate (default 1.0).

positional arguments:
  blueprint             blueprint file (YAML or JSON) or project folder
  dataset               dataset file (.yaml, .yml or .json)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --tools FILES         more tool files or modules, comma-separated (repeatable); the tools.py
                        next to the blueprint is always loaded
  --skills DIR          more skill folders (repeatable); skills/ next to the blueprint is always
                        loaded
  --agent NAME          evaluate this one agent of the blueprint instead of its entrypoint (for
                        example a judge, with verdict:<decision> scorers)
  --scorer SPEC         scorer applied to every case, e.g. contains, tool:lookup_order,
                        max_tokens:20000 (repeatable)
  --tag TAG             only cases with this tag (repeatable)
  --case ID             only the case with this id (repeatable; combines with --tag)
  --concurrency N       runs in flight (default 4)
  --repetitions N       runs per case (default 1)
  --timeout SECONDS     seconds per run before it is cancelled
  --max-requests N      model calls for each run; a larger value in the blueprint's limits wins
  --max-total-tokens N  prompt plus completion tokens for each run; a larger value in the
                        blueprint's limits wins
  --max-tool-calls N    tool calls for each run; a larger value in the blueprint's limits wins
  --max-cost AMOUNT     cost (needs prices) for each run; a larger value in the blueprint's limits
                        wins
  --max-duration TIME   longest time, e.g. 5m, for each run; a larger value in the blueprint's
                        limits wins
  --sandbox DIR         folder whose subfolders every case gets a fresh copy of (default: data/,
                        out/ and the workspace folders next to the blueprint)
  --no-sandbox          run every case on the files in place (cases may see each other's writes)
  --judge-model MODEL   model for judge:<criteria> scorers
  --fail-fast           stop at the first failure
  --json FILE           write the report as JSON to FILE
  --markdown FILE       also write the report as Markdown to FILE
  --format {text,markdown}
                        what is printed: text, tables aligned for the terminal (default), or
                        Markdown
  --baseline FILE       compare with this JSON report
  --min-pass-rate RATE  fail (exit 1) below this pass rate (default 1.0)
  --min-pass-hat-k R    fail (exit 1) when fewer than this share of cases passed every repetition
                        (pass^k; needs --repetitions 2 or more)
  --cost-budget AMOUNT  fail (exit 1) when the whole evaluation costs more than this (needs
                        prices)
  --prices FILE         YAML file with your model prices (per million tokens) to report the cost
  --tolerance DROP      allowed drop of a mean score against the baseline (default 0.1)
  --replay              record model responses and answer unchanged calls from them on the next
                        run (stand-in tools only; see --replay-store)
  --replay-store FILE   SQLite file of recorded responses (default .awa/replay.db next to the
                        blueprint)
  --search-fixture FILE
                        answer web searches from this JSON file of recorded results (live without
                        it)
  --record-search       with --search-fixture: search live for queries the file lacks and add them
  --deps JSON           deps for every run: a JSON object, or @file.json (tools read them from the
                        run context)
  --user-id ID          the user the runs act for, added to the deps as user_id (user-scoped
                        memory)
```

### `awa data`

```text
usage: awa data [-h] action ...

[preview] Work with your files: see what is in them (changes nothing), check them against a
project, run a project on them, and declare the databases and APIs it uses.

positional arguments:
  action
    inspect        show what is in your files and what awa made of them
    check          test a project's `data:` section against the files on disk
    run            run a project built with --data on its input files; results go to data/output/
    add-system     declare a database or API the process uses: test it read-only, save its
                   settings in .env and read its structure
    remove-system  forget a declared system (its settings stay in .env)

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
```

#### `awa data inspect`

```text
usage: awa data inspect [-h] [--json | --model-view] [--out FILE] [--force]
                        [--mask {none,placeholders,drop}] [--budget N] [--no-samples]
                        [--max-file-mb MB] [--strict]
                        files [files ...]

Show what is in your files (tables, columns, pages, personal data) and what awa made of them;
changes nothing. Exit code 1 on errors (--strict: on warnings).

positional arguments:
  files                 files, folders (recursive) and glob patterns; a project folder also shows
                        its declared external systems

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --json                print the profile as JSON
  --model-view          print exactly what a model would see (a short, budgeted digest)
  --out FILE            also write the profile JSON to FILE
  --force               overwrite an existing --out file
  --mask {none,placeholders,drop}
                        what the model view shows of personal data: nothing hidden (default),
                        consistent placeholders like <IBAN_1>, or no sample values; `drop` also
                        strips the JSON
  --budget N            size of the model view in tokens (default 6000)
  --no-samples          leave out every value taken from the files (rows, examples, excerpts)
  --max-file-mb MB      larger files are reported as errors (default 100)
  --strict              exit with code 1 on any warning, not only on errors
```

#### `awa data check`

```text
usage: awa data check [-h] [--json] project

Check a project's `data:` section against the files on disk. Exit code 1 when a file is missing or
no longer matches.

positional arguments:
  project     a project folder (with blueprint.yaml) or a blueprint file with a `data:` section

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print the result as JSON
```

#### `awa data run`

```text
usage: awa data run [-h] (--file NAME | --all) [--model MODEL] [--json] [--no-input]
                    [--tools FILES] [--skills DIR] [--max-requests N] [--max-total-tokens N]
                    [--max-tool-calls N] [--max-cost AMOUNT] [--max-duration TIME]
                    project

Run a project built with --data on its input files; the results go to data/output/. Needs a model
key (awa setup sets it, awa doctor checks it). Exit code 2 when a run waits for an approval.

positional arguments:
  project               project folder (or its blueprint.yaml)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file NAME           an input file or glob (matched against the name below data/files/),
                        repeatable
  --all                 run on every input file (refused when several files exist and none is
                        marked role: reference: name them with --file)
  --model MODEL         model profile or provider:model for every agent
  --json                print the outcomes as JSON
  --no-input            never ask for approvals: a run that needs one ends paused (exit code 2)
  --tools FILES         more tool files or modules, comma-separated (repeatable); the tools.py
                        next to the blueprint is always loaded
  --skills DIR          more skill folders (repeatable); skills/ next to the blueprint is always
                        loaded
  --max-requests N      model calls for each run; can only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-total-tokens N  prompt plus completion tokens for each run; can only tighten the
                        blueprint's limits
  --max-tool-calls N    tool calls for each run; can only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-cost AMOUNT     cost (needs prices) for each run; can only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-duration TIME   longest time, e.g. 5m, for each run; can only tighten the blueprint's
                        limits
```

#### `awa data add-system`

```text
usage: awa data add-system [-h] --type KIND --name NAME [--key KEY] [--samples] [--no-input]
                           project

Declare a database or API the process uses: test it read-only, save its settings in the project
.env and read its structure.

positional arguments:
  project      project folder (created when missing)

options:
  -h, --help   show this help message and exit
  --type KIND  the kind of system: sql (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQL Server), openapi (a
               REST API with an OpenAPI description), or another connector of `awa connectors
               list`
  --name NAME  your name for it, e.g. "Invoice ledger"
  --key KEY    its short id in blueprint.yaml (default: from the name)
  --samples    also read up to 3 example rows per table for the design (masked like your files)
  --no-input   never ask: use only settings already in DIR/.env or the environment
```

#### `awa data remove-system`

```text
usage: awa data remove-system [-h] project key

Forget a declared system; its settings stay in .env.

positional arguments:
  project     project folder
  key         the system's id (shown by `awa data inspect DIR`)

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

### `awa doctor`

```text
usage: awa doctor [-h] [--json] [--check-models] [--check-postgres] [--check-langfuse]

Check Python, the virtual environment, the awa install, extras, credentials and settings, and show
where each setting comes from. Exit code 1 when something blocks use, 78 when a required part is
missing (a model key, or a variable a trigger needs).

options:
  -h, --help        show this help message and exit
  --json            print the report as JSON
  --check-models    make one tiny real call per model profile (costs tokens)
  --check-postgres  connect to AWA_POSTGRES_DSN
  --check-langfuse  ask the Langfuse server for its health and check the keys (sends no trace)
```

### `awa check`

```text
usage: awa check [-h] [--allow-post {teams}] [--no-model] [--project DIR] [--json] [GROUP ...]

[preview] Check the Microsoft 365 setup with small read-only calls and say how to fix what is red.

positional arguments:
  GROUP                 microsoft or all (default all; both run the Microsoft 365 checks)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --allow-post {teams}  allow ONE test message (teams: a card through the webhook or to the pinned
                        channel)
  --no-model            check the Azure OpenAI route without calling it
  --project DIR         project folder with .env (default .)
  --json                print the report as JSON
```

## Run

### `awa chat`

```text
usage: awa chat [-h] [--thread-id THREAD_ID] [--stream | --no-stream] [--tools FILES]
                [--skills DIR] [--deps JSON] [--user-id ID] [--max-requests N]
                [--max-total-tokens N] [--max-tool-calls N] [--max-cost AMOUNT]
                [--max-duration TIME]
                blueprint

Talk to the system in the terminal; tool calls that need an approval are asked inline. A team or
single agent keeps the conversation; a workflow or network answers each message on its own. Needs
a model key (awa setup sets it, awa doctor checks it). /help lists the chat commands.

positional arguments:
  blueprint             blueprint file (YAML or JSON) or project folder

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --thread-id THREAD_ID
                        thread id to start on (kept in memory for this chat)
  --stream, --no-stream
                        print replies as they are written, with event lines (default: on)
  --tools FILES         more tool files or modules, comma-separated (repeatable); the tools.py
                        next to the blueprint is always loaded
  --skills DIR          more skill folders (repeatable); skills/ next to the blueprint is always
                        loaded
  --deps JSON           deps for every run: a JSON object, or @file.json (tools read them from the
                        run context)
  --user-id ID          the user the runs act for, added to the deps as user_id (user-scoped
                        memory)
  --max-requests N      model calls for each turn; can only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-total-tokens N  prompt plus completion tokens for each turn; can only tighten the
                        blueprint's limits
  --max-tool-calls N    tool calls for each turn; can only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-cost AMOUNT     cost (needs prices) for each turn; can only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-duration TIME   longest time, e.g. 5m, for each turn; can only tighten the blueprint's
                        limits
```

### `awa run`

```text
usage: awa run [-h] [--stream] [--thread-id ID] [--json] [--trace [FILE]]
               [--trace-level {summary,full}] [--tools FILES] [--skills DIR] [--deps JSON]
               [--user-id ID] [--max-requests N] [--max-total-tokens N] [--max-tool-calls N]
               [--max-cost AMOUNT] [--max-duration TIME]
               blueprint task

Give the system one task and print the answer, with --stream also each event. Needs a model key
(awa setup sets it, awa doctor checks it). Exit code 2 when the run waits for an approval (answer
it in awa chat).

positional arguments:
  blueprint             blueprint file (YAML or JSON) or project folder
  task                  the task or message for the system

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --stream              print events as they happen
  --thread-id ID        thread id for the run (state lives in memory for this invocation only)
  --json                print the result as JSON
  --trace [FILE]        write the run's trace (agents, tools, delegations, approvals, tokens;
                        secrets redacted) to FILE, default .awa/traces/RUN_ID.jsonl; read it with
                        `awa runs trace`
  --trace-level {summary,full}
                        what --trace records: summary (no message texts) or full (default summary)
  --tools FILES         more tool files or modules, comma-separated (repeatable); the tools.py
                        next to the blueprint is always loaded
  --skills DIR          more skill folders (repeatable); skills/ next to the blueprint is always
                        loaded
  --deps JSON           deps for every run: a JSON object, or @file.json (tools read them from the
                        run context)
  --user-id ID          the user the runs act for, added to the deps as user_id (user-scoped
                        memory)
  --max-requests N      model calls for each run; can only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-total-tokens N  prompt plus completion tokens for each run; can only tighten the
                        blueprint's limits
  --max-tool-calls N    tool calls for each run; can only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-cost AMOUNT     cost (needs prices) for each run; can only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-duration TIME   longest time, e.g. 5m, for each run; can only tighten the blueprint's
                        limits
```

### `awa worker`

```text
usage: awa worker [-h] [--tools FILES] [--skills DIR] [--max-requests N] [--max-total-tokens N]
                  [--max-tool-calls N] [--max-cost AMOUNT] [--max-duration TIME] [--dsn DSN]
                  [--schema SCHEMA] [--store FILE] [--concurrency N] [--lease SECONDS]
                  [--trace-level {off,summary,full}] [--drain-timeout SECONDS] [--no-triggers]
                  [--once]
                  target

[preview] Run the automations of a project until stopped (Ctrl+C), without a web server: fire its
triggers (schedule, file drop, email, queue), execute queued process runs, retry, recover runs of
crashed workers and send SLA reminders. Needs a model key (awa setup). With --once: exit code 1
when a run failed, 2 when runs wait.

positional arguments:
  target                blueprint file or project folder

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --tools FILES         more tool files or modules, comma-separated (repeatable); the tools.py
                        next to the blueprint is always loaded
  --skills DIR          more skill folders (repeatable); skills/ next to the blueprint is always
                        loaded
  --max-requests N      model calls for each process run; can only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-total-tokens N  prompt plus completion tokens for each process run; can only tighten the
                        blueprint's limits
  --max-tool-calls N    tool calls for each process run; can only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-cost AMOUNT     cost (needs prices) for each process run; can only tighten the blueprint's
                        limits
  --max-duration TIME   longest time, e.g. 5m, for each process run; can only tighten the
                        blueprint's limits
  --dsn DSN             PostgreSQL address of the runs (default: $AWA_POSTGRES_DSN)
  --schema SCHEMA       PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
  --store FILE          local data file without a DSN (default .awa/awa.db next to the blueprint,
                        else in this folder; checkpoints are kept beside it in checkpoints.db)
  --concurrency N       most runs at once in this worker (default: the sum of the automations'
                        `concurrency`; each automation's own limit still applies across all
                        workers)
  --lease SECONDS       how long a run stays claimed by this worker without a sign of life
                        (default 300)
  --trace-level {off,summary,full}
                        how much each run's trace records: summary (no message texts), full or off
                        (default: $AWA_TRACE_LEVEL, else summary)
  --drain-timeout SECONDS
                        seconds runs in flight get to finish at shutdown (default 30)
  --no-triggers         only execute queued runs
  --once                handle what is ready now (trigger events, queued runs), then exit
```

### `awa serve`

```text
usage: awa serve [-h] [--tools FILES] [--skills DIR] [--max-requests N] [--max-total-tokens N]
                 [--max-tool-calls N] [--max-cost AMOUNT] [--max-duration TIME] [--host HOST]
                 [--port PORT] [--allowed-host HOST] [--docs] [--allow-unauthenticated]
                 [--api-key-env VAR | --api-keys-file FILE] [--cors-origin ORIGIN]
                 [--thread-scope {tenant,principal,shared}] [--rate-limit N/SECONDS]
                 [--max-concurrency N] [--approver-role ROLE] [--drain-timeout SECONDS]
                 [--max-body-bytes N] [--log-format {text,json}] [--dsn DSN] [--schema SCHEMA]
                 [--store STORE] [--log-level {critical,error,warning,info,debug,trace}]
                 blueprint

[preview] Offer the system as a web API (HTTP, server-sent events), receive its webhooks and run
its other triggers. Paused runs are kept in .awa/ next to the blueprint, or in PostgreSQL with
--dsn. Needs a model key (awa setup sets it, awa doctor checks it). Needs the server extra (awa
doctor prints the install command).

positional arguments:
  blueprint             blueprint file (YAML or JSON) or project folder

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --tools FILES         more tool files or modules, comma-separated (repeatable); the tools.py
                        next to the blueprint is always loaded
  --skills DIR          more skill folders (repeatable); skills/ next to the blueprint is always
                        loaded
  --max-requests N      model calls for each request and automation run; can only tighten the
                        blueprint's limits
  --max-total-tokens N  prompt plus completion tokens for each request and automation run; can
                        only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-tool-calls N    tool calls for each request and automation run; can only tighten the
                        blueprint's limits
  --max-cost AMOUNT     cost (needs prices) for each request and automation run; can only tighten
                        the blueprint's limits
  --max-duration TIME   longest time, e.g. 5m, for each request and automation run; can only
                        tighten the blueprint's limits
  --host HOST           interface to bind (default 127.0.0.1)
  --port PORT           port to listen on (default 8000)
  --allowed-host HOST   host name the server answers besides its own (repeatable; default: the
                        comma-separated AWA_ALLOWED_HOSTS; without an API key other Host headers
                        are refused)
  --docs                serve the OpenAPI document at /openapi.json (needs the API key when one is
                        set)
  --allow-unauthenticated
                        allow a non-loopback --host without an API key (anyone who can reach the
                        port can run the system)
  --api-key-env VAR     environment variable holding the API key clients must send as a bearer
                        token
  --api-keys-file FILE  JSON file mapping API key digests (or key variables) to principals and
                        tenants
  --cors-origin ORIGIN  browser origin allowed to call the API (repeatable)
  --thread-scope {tenant,principal,shared}
                        who may use a thread: its tenant (default), its creator, or anyone
  --rate-limit N/SECONDS
                        requests (runs and resumes) per principal, e.g. 60/60
  --max-concurrency N   runs in flight at once; further requests get 503
  --approver-role ROLE  role needed to answer approvals (repeatable; default: any caller)
  --drain-timeout SECONDS
                        seconds runs in flight get to finish at shutdown (default 30)
  --max-body-bytes N    largest request body accepted (default 1 MiB)
  --log-format {text,json}
                        text (default) or JSON lines with request ids
  --dsn DSN             PostgreSQL DSN keeping automation runs and paused runs, shared with `awa
                        worker` and `awa runs` (default: $AWA_POSTGRES_DSN; without one they are
                        kept in .awa/ next to the blueprint)
  --schema SCHEMA       PostgreSQL schema of the run tables (default awa)
  --store STORE         without a DSN: the local data file (default .awa/awa.db next to the
                        blueprint; the checkpoints are kept beside it in checkpoints.db)
  --log-level {critical,error,warning,info,debug,trace}
                        uvicorn log level
```

### `awa mcp`

```text
usage: awa mcp [-h] action ...

Use the system with MCP: pin the tool definitions of its MCP servers, list them, or offer the
system itself as an MCP server.

positional arguments:
  action
    lock      pin the tool definitions in mcp.lock.json
    list      list the tools and their pin status
    serve     [preview] offer a blueprint's system to MCP clients

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

#### `awa mcp lock`

```text
usage: awa mcp lock [-h] [--server SERVER] [--output OUTPUT] [--tools] blueprint

Connect to the blueprint's MCP servers and write their tool definitions to mcp.lock.json, so a
changed tool is noticed before it is used.

positional arguments:
  blueprint            blueprint file (YAML or JSON) or project folder

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --server SERVER      only this server (repeatable)
  --output, -o OUTPUT  lock file to write (default: mcp.lock.json next to it)
  --tools              also record each tool's description and input schema, for reviewable diffs
```

#### `awa mcp list`

```text
usage: awa mcp list [-h] [--server SERVER] [--lock LOCK] blueprint

List the tools of the blueprint's MCP servers and whether each matches the pin in mcp.lock.json.
Exit code 1 when a tool changed or is not pinned.

positional arguments:
  blueprint        blueprint file (YAML or JSON) or project folder

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --server SERVER  only this server (repeatable)
  --lock LOCK      compare with this lock file instead
```

#### `awa mcp serve`

```text
usage: awa mcp serve [-h] [--tools FILES] [--skills DIR] [--expose-tools]
                     [--transport {stdio,http}] [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--path PATH]
                     [--api-key-env VAR] [--allow-unauthenticated] [--no-elicit]
                     blueprint

[preview] Offer the system as an MCP server (stdio by default, or http), so MCP clients can send
it tasks. Needs a model key (awa setup sets it, awa doctor checks it).

positional arguments:
  blueprint             blueprint file (YAML or JSON) or project folder

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --tools FILES         more tool files or modules, comma-separated (repeatable); the tools.py
                        next to the blueprint is always loaded
  --skills DIR          more skill folders (repeatable); skills/ next to the blueprint is always
                        loaded
  --expose-tools        also expose the loaded tools that need no approval as MCP tools
  --transport {stdio,http}
                        stdio (default) or http
  --host HOST           interface for http (default 127.0.0.1)
  --port PORT           port for http (default 8000)
  --path PATH           endpoint path for http (default /mcp)
  --api-key-env VAR     environment variable holding the bearer key http clients must send
  --allow-unauthenticated
                        allow http on a non-loopback --host without --api-key-env (anyone who can
                        reach the port can run the system)
  --no-elicit           never ask the client's user for approvals; return interrupted results
```

## Operate

### `awa runs`

```text
usage: awa runs [-h] action ...

[preview] List and operate the process runs of a project: the same store awa worker and awa serve
use (.awa/awa.db next to the blueprint, or PostgreSQL with --dsn).

positional arguments:
  action
    list          list process runs, newest first
    show          show one run with its history (--steps: its steps, attempts and results in
                  order)
    retry         queue a failed or dead-lettered run again
    cancel        cancel an unfinished run
    decide        approve or reject a run waiting for an approval
    trace         show what a run did: agents, tools, delegations, approvals, tokens, cost, errors
    export-cases  turn finished runs into eval cases (a regression test from a real run)
    dlq           list the dead-lettered runs
    migrate       move waiting runs of older versions to the blueprint's current version

options:
  -h, --help      show this help message and exit
```

#### `awa runs list`

```text
usage: awa runs list [-h] [--automation AUTOMATION] [--status STATUS] [--limit N] [--json]
                     [--dsn DSN] [--schema SCHEMA] [--store FILE]
                     [PROJECT|BLUEPRINT]

List the process runs, newest first, with their status.

positional arguments:
  PROJECT|BLUEPRINT     the project folder or blueprint whose runs to show (default: the project
                        of the current folder); the same store `awa worker` and `awa serve` use

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --automation AUTOMATION
                        only this automation
  --status STATUS       only this status (repeatable)
  --limit N             most runs to show (default 50)
  --json                print JSON
  --dsn DSN             PostgreSQL address of the runs (default: $AWA_POSTGRES_DSN)
  --schema SCHEMA       PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
  --store FILE          local data file without a DSN (default .awa/awa.db next to the blueprint,
                        else in this folder; checkpoints are kept beside it in checkpoints.db)
```

#### `awa runs show`

```text
usage: awa runs show [-h] [--steps] [--dsn DSN] [--schema SCHEMA] [--store FILE] run_id

Show one run: its status, input, output, waits and history.

positional arguments:
  run_id           the run's id (see awa runs list)

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --steps          add the steps in order, each with its attempts (status, time, tokens, cost),
                   results (output, tool calls, checks) and approvals (reviewer, reason)
  --dsn DSN        PostgreSQL address of the runs (default: $AWA_POSTGRES_DSN)
  --schema SCHEMA  PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
  --store FILE     local data file without a DSN (default .awa/awa.db next to the blueprint, else
                   in this folder; checkpoints are kept beside it in checkpoints.db)
```

#### `awa runs retry`

```text
usage: awa runs retry [-h] [--actor ACTOR] [--restart] [--dsn DSN] [--schema SCHEMA]
                      [--store FILE]
                      run_id

Queue a failed or dead-lettered run again; a running worker picks it up.

positional arguments:
  run_id           the run's id (see awa runs list)

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --actor ACTOR    who retries it (recorded)
  --restart        start again from the input instead of resuming where the run stopped (automatic
                   when its paused state is lost)
  --dsn DSN        PostgreSQL address of the runs (default: $AWA_POSTGRES_DSN)
  --schema SCHEMA  PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
  --store FILE     local data file without a DSN (default .awa/awa.db next to the blueprint, else
                   in this folder; checkpoints are kept beside it in checkpoints.db)
```

#### `awa runs cancel`

```text
usage: awa runs cancel [-h] [--reason REASON] [--actor ACTOR] [--dsn DSN] [--schema SCHEMA]
                       [--store FILE]
                       run_id

Cancel a run that has not finished; the reason is stored with it.

positional arguments:
  run_id           the run's id (see awa runs list)

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --reason REASON  why; stored with the run (default: cancelled by operator)
  --actor ACTOR    who cancels it (recorded)
  --dsn DSN        PostgreSQL address of the runs (default: $AWA_POSTGRES_DSN)
  --schema SCHEMA  PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
  --store FILE     local data file without a DSN (default .awa/awa.db next to the blueprint, else
                   in this folder; checkpoints are kept beside it in checkpoints.db)
```

#### `awa runs decide`

```text
usage: awa runs decide [-h] (--approve | --reject) [--note NOTE] [--edit-args JSON]
                       [--interrupt-id INTERRUPT_ID] [--actor ACTOR] [--dsn DSN] [--schema SCHEMA]
                       [--store FILE]
                       run_id

Answer the approval a process run waits for (the oldest open one, unless --interrupt-id names
another). The decision is recorded in the run store; once every approval of the run is answered it
is queued, and `awa worker` or `awa serve` using the same store resumes it, also after a restart.
Use the same --dsn, or run the command in the blueprint's folder (or pass the same --store).

positional arguments:
  run_id                the waiting run (see `awa runs list --status waiting`)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --approve             let the tool call run
  --reject              refuse the tool call
  --note NOTE           reason or comment recorded with it
  --edit-args JSON      with --approve: run the call with these arguments instead (JSON object or
                        @file)
  --interrupt-id INTERRUPT_ID
                        which approval, when the run waits for several
  --actor ACTOR         the approver (recorded as reviewer)
  --dsn DSN             PostgreSQL address of the runs (default: $AWA_POSTGRES_DSN)
  --schema SCHEMA       PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
  --store FILE          local data file without a DSN (default .awa/awa.db next to the blueprint,
                        else in this folder; checkpoints are kept beside it in checkpoints.db)
```

#### `awa runs trace`

```text
usage: awa runs trace [-h] [--attempt ATTEMPT | --all] [--json] [--prices FILE] [--store STORE]
                      [--traces DIR]
                      run_id

Print the trace of a process run as a tree: the agents, what each of them called, delegated or
asked for, with model calls, tokens, cost, time and errors per step. Traces are written by `awa
worker`, `awa serve` and `awa run --trace` in .awa/traces next to the run store; use the same
folder, or pass --traces or --store.

positional arguments:
  run_id             the process run, or a trace file (.jsonl)

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --attempt ATTEMPT  show attempt N (default: the last one)
  --all              show every attempt
  --json             print the tree as JSON
  --prices FILE      model prices to show the cost (default: the trace's own)
  --store STORE      local run store whose folder holds the traces (default .awa/awa.db)
  --traces DIR       folder of the trace files (default: traces/ beside the run store)
```

#### `awa runs export-cases`

```text
usage: awa runs export-cases [-h] --out FILE [--no-judge] [--dsn DSN] [--schema SCHEMA]
                             [--store FILE] [--traces DIR]
                             run_id [run_id ...]

Write one eval case per succeeded run: its input, the decisions taken at its approvals, `tool:`
and `delegated:` expectations from its trace, and its output as the reference of a `judge:`
scorer. Run the file with `awa eval`. Cases already in the file are kept as they are.

positional arguments:
  run_id           succeeded process runs

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --out FILE       dataset file (.yaml)
  --no-judge       no judge scorer (only tools and delegations)
  --dsn DSN        PostgreSQL address of the runs (default: $AWA_POSTGRES_DSN)
  --schema SCHEMA  PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
  --store FILE     local data file without a DSN (default .awa/awa.db next to the blueprint, else
                   in this folder; checkpoints are kept beside it in checkpoints.db)
  --traces DIR     folder of the trace files (default: traces/ beside the run store)
```

#### `awa runs dlq`

```text
                    [--schema SCHEMA] [--store FILE]

```

#### `awa runs migrate`

#### `awa trigger run`

```text
usage: awa trigger run [-h] [--payload PAYLOAD] [--dry-run] [--json] [--tools FILES]
                       [--skills DIR] [--max-requests N] [--max-total-tokens N]
                       [--max-tool-calls N] [--max-cost AMOUNT] [--max-duration TIME]
                       blueprint trigger

Fire a trigger once with --payload and run the process here; --dry-run only shows the task it
would get. Exit code 2 when the run waits for an approval.

positional arguments:
  blueprint             blueprint file or project folder
  trigger               trigger name

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --payload PAYLOAD     payload as JSON, or @file.json (default {})
  --dry-run             only show the input, thread id and dedup key (builds no agents, needs no
                        settings)
  --json                print the run as JSON
  --tools FILES         more tool files or modules, comma-separated (repeatable); the tools.py
                        next to the blueprint is always loaded
  --skills DIR          more skill folders (repeatable); skills/ next to the blueprint is always
                        loaded
  --max-requests N      model calls for each process run; can only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-total-tokens N  prompt plus completion tokens for each process run; can only tighten the
                        blueprint's limits
  --max-tool-calls N    tool calls for each process run; can only tighten the blueprint's limits
  --max-cost AMOUNT     cost (needs prices) for each process run; can only tighten the blueprint's
                        limits
  --max-duration TIME   longest time, e.g. 5m, for each process run; can only tighten the
                        blueprint's limits
```

### `awa plugins`

```text
usage: awa plugins [-h] action ...

Plugins add tools, connectors, skills, models, parsers and erasure handlers. They come from the

are only switches (guard.*, cache.*, tracer.*) are listed too.

positional arguments:
  action
    list      list every plugin and part
    show      show one plugin or part
    check     run the contract test of a part (offline)
    switch    switch a part on or off in the blueprint's components: section

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

#### `awa plugins list`

```text
usage: awa plugins list [-h] [--kind KIND] [--json]

List every plugin (project folder, installed packages, built-in) and switchable part. Installed
plugins are not imported; the project folder's Python files are, as when the project runs.

options:
  -h, --help   show this help message and exit
  --kind KIND  only this kind (tools, parsers, skill, guard, ...)
  --json       print the rows as JSON
```

#### `awa plugins show`

```text
usage: awa plugins show [-h] [--json] KIND.NAME

Show one plugin or part: source, status, switch key.

positional arguments:
  KIND.NAME   as awa plugins list shows it

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print the rows as JSON
```

#### `awa plugins check`

```text
module:Object). Exit code 1 when it fails.

  KIND.NAME             a parser, connector, tool or sql_guard

  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --target module:Object
                        test this replacement instead
```

## Settings

### `awa env`

```text
usage: awa env [-h] action ...

Show and change the settings in the project .env. A value is taken from the environment, else the
project .env, else the default. Secret values are never shown: only whether they are set.

positional arguments:
  action
    list      show every setting with its value, source and users
    get       show one setting and where its value comes from
    set       check a value and write it to the project .env
    unset     remove a setting from the project .env

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

#### `awa env list`

```text
usage: awa env list [-h] [--group GROUP] [--json]

Show every setting with its value, source and users. Secret values show only "set" or "not set".

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
  --group GROUP  only this group (models, azure, storage, ...)
  --json         print the settings as JSON
```

#### `awa env get`

```text
usage: awa env get [-h] [--json] name

Show one setting and where its value comes from (env, .env:<line> or default).

positional arguments:
  name        the setting, e.g. AWA_DEFAULT_MODEL

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print the setting as JSON
```

#### `awa env set`

```text
usage: awa env set [-h] [--stdin] [--confirm] NAME[=VALUE]

Check the value and write it to the project .env. Secret settings never accept NAME=VALUE: type
the value hidden, or pass it with --stdin. Security switches and endpoint or base-URL settings
need --confirm.

positional arguments:
  NAME[=VALUE]  the setting and its value; a secret takes only NAME (its value is asked hidden)

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit
  --stdin       read the value from standard input
  --confirm     confirm a security switch or a request address
```

#### `awa env unset`

```text
usage: awa env unset [-h] name

Remove a setting from the project .env.

positional arguments:
  name        the setting to remove

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

#### `awa cache clear`

```text
usage: awa cache clear [-h] [--tenant TENANT] [--kind KIND] [--replay] [--replay-store FILE]
                       [project]

Delete cache entries: all, or one tenant or kind; --replay the recordings of awa eval --replay.

positional arguments:
  project              project folder or blueprint (default .)

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --tenant TENANT      only this tenant
  --kind KIND          only this kind (tools, steps, examples, plans)
  --replay             the recordings of awa eval --replay
  --replay-store FILE  recordings file (default .awa/replay.db)
```

#### `awa cache salt`

```text
usage: awa cache salt [-h] [--force] [project]

Write a random AWA_CACHE_SALT into the project's .env, so cache keys stay stable across processes
(the value is never shown).

positional arguments:
  project     project folder or blueprint (default .)

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --force     replace a salt that is already set
```

### `awa store`

```text
usage: awa store [-h] action ...

[preview] Where process runs, steps and results are kept: the project's SQLite file (.awa/awa.db)
or PostgreSQL. Show it, switch it, back it up, erase or sweep old runs.

positional arguments:
  action
    status    the active store, its schema and row counts
    use       make sqlite or postgres the store: move the data, verify it, switch
    migrate   the move of `use`, with every option
    upgrade   apply pending schema migrations
    backup    back up the local data (SQLite backup API)
    erase     delete runs for good: one run, an automation's runs, or a person's
    sweep     delete finished runs older than the retention

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

#### `awa store status`

```text
usage: awa store status [-h] [--schema SCHEMA] [--json] [project]

Show the active store, its schema version and the row counts.

positional arguments:
  project          project folder (default: --project, else .)

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --schema SCHEMA  PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
  --json           print the status as JSON
```

#### `awa store use`

```text
usage: awa store use [-h] [--schema SCHEMA] {postgres,sqlite} [project]

Move the project's runs, steps, results, thread owners and checkpoints into the other store,
verify counts and checksums, then set AWA_DATA_BACKEND in .env. `use postgres` without
AWA_POSTGRES_DSN starts the local PostgreSQL in Docker first (as `awa setup` does). The old store
stays untouched as a backup.

positional arguments:
  {postgres,sqlite}  the store to move to
  project            project folder (default: --project, else .)

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --schema SCHEMA    PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
```

#### `awa store migrate`

```text
usage: awa store migrate [-h] --to {postgres,sqlite} [--dsn-env NAME] [--dry-run] [--no-switch]
                         [--json] [--schema SCHEMA]
                         [project]

The move of `store use` with every option (--dry-run counts only).

positional arguments:
  project               project folder (default: --project, else .)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --to {postgres,sqlite}
                        the store to move to
  --dsn-env NAME        variable holding the DSN
  --dry-run             only count what would move (copies no row; the stores are still prepared)
  --no-switch           copy and verify, but keep AWA_DATA_BACKEND
  --json                print the result as JSON
  --schema SCHEMA       PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
```

#### `awa store upgrade`

```text
usage: awa store upgrade [-h] [--schema SCHEMA] [project]

Apply pending schema migrations (servers and workers also do it on start).

positional arguments:
  project          project folder (default: --project, else .)

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --schema SCHEMA  PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
```

#### `awa store backup`

```text
usage: awa store backup [-h] [--schema SCHEMA] target [project]

Back up the local SQLite data into a new folder (PostgreSQL: see the docs).

positional arguments:
  target           a new folder for the backup files
  project          project folder (default: --project, else .)

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --schema SCHEMA  PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
```

#### `awa store erase`

```text
usage: awa store erase [-h] --automation AUTOMATION [--tenant TENANT] (--run RUN | --all |
                       --person PERSON) [--confirm] [--schema SCHEMA]
                       [project]

Delete runs for good: one run, every run of an automation, or every run a person started or
decided on; --all and --person need --confirm.

positional arguments:
  project               project folder (default: --project, else .)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --automation AUTOMATION
                        the automation (project) name
  --tenant TENANT       the tenant (default local)
  --run RUN             one process run
  --all                 every run of the automation
  --person PERSON       every run this principal started or decided on
  --confirm             confirm deleting many runs (--all, --person)
  --schema SCHEMA       PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
```

#### `awa store sweep`

```text
usage: awa store sweep [-h] [--days DAYS] [--schema SCHEMA] [project]

Delete finished runs older than the retention (AWA_RUN_RETENTION_DAYS).

positional arguments:
  project          project folder (default: --project, else .)

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --days DAYS      default: AWA_RUN_RETENTION_DAYS (at least 1)
  --schema SCHEMA  PostgreSQL schema (default awa)
```

## Templates of `awa init`

| Template | The system |
| --- | --- |
| `minimal` | One agent that answers account questions and opens follow-up tickets; every ticket waits for a human. |
| `team` | An orchestrator that delegates research and writing to team members; publishing a brief waits for a human. |
| `workflow` | A fixed review workflow: intake, parallel policy and risk checks, and a structured verdict. |
| `network` | A lead that plans tasks on a board and teammates that work on them concurrently; scheduling a post waits for a human. |
| `support` | A customer-support desk: triage delegates order questions and hands refunds to a refunds agent; every refund waits for a human. |

<!-- end of generated commands -->

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Done. |
| 1 | Something failed: a run, a test below its target, an invalid file. |
| 2 | A run waits: for an approval that could not be asked for here, or for an event. |
| 3 | A change needs a confirmation that was not given: `--confirm`, `--yes` or a typed name. |
| 4 | `awa export` refused the project: every feature it does not carry over is listed, and nothing was written. |
| 78 | The configuration is incomplete: a model key, a variable a trigger needs, or a database that does not answer. Each problem is one line `problem: ... -- fix: ...`. |
| 130 | Interrupted with Ctrl+C. |

<!-- source: reference/settings.md -->

# Settings

<!-- Generated from the settings registry by scripts/gen_settings.py: do not edit. -->

Every setting awa reads, with its environment variable and default, generated from the
code.

```console
awa env list                          # every setting, its value and where it comes from
awa env set AWA_TRACE_LEVEL=full      # write one into the project .env
```

A value is taken from the process environment, else from the project `.env`, else the
default ([Configuration](../develop/configuration.md)). awa never shows a secret value.
A setting marked *confirm* decides where requests go or switches a protection:
`awa env set` needs `--confirm` for it.

## Model profiles

| Variable | What it does | Values (default) | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AWA_DEFAULT_MODEL` | Model of the `default` profile (`provider:model`). Unset: chosen from the provider whose credentials are set. | text (`anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5`) | awa.models |
| `AWA_FAST_MODEL` | Model of the `fast` profile. Unset: chosen from the provider whose credentials are set. | text (`anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5`) | awa.models |
| `AWA_STRONG_MODEL` | Model of the `strong` profile. Unset: chosen from the provider whose credentials are set. | text (`anthropic:claude-opus-5-5`) | awa.models |
| `AWA_OPENAI_RESPONSES_API` | Send OpenAI and Azure OpenAI reasoning models that get an effort (judge and reviewer `low`, worker `medium`) through the Responses API, the API that takes an effort together with tools, with `store=False` (no response kept by the provider; the reasoning travels encrypted). `false`: Chat Completions without an effort. A model's own `use_responses_api` or `store` setting wins. | `true`, `false` (`false`) | awa.models |
| `AWA_VISION_MODEL` | Model that reads scanned PDF pages (a profile or `provider:model`, e.g. `fast`). Unset: the `default` profile; the workspace `ocr` option overrides it. | text | vision OCR of scanned PDF pages, workspace connector |

## Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365 (Outlook, SharePoint and Excel, Teams)

| Variable | What it does | Values (default) | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AZURE_TENANT_ID` | Directory (tenant) ID of the one app registration (Entra admin center > App registrations > Overview), also for Azure OpenAI with AZURE_OPENAI_AUTH=entra. Permission: none itself; each service below names its own. | text | awa.models, connectors outlook, sharepoint, teams, microsoft_graph, awa check, awa people |
| `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` | Application (client) ID (a GUID) of that app. Permission: none itself; its API permissions are listed per service below. Check everything with `awa check microsoft`. Finding people (`awa people`, role: recipients): application User.Read.All with admin consent. | text | awa.models, connectors outlook, sharepoint, teams, microsoft_graph, awa check, awa people |
| `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` | A client secret of the app: Certificates & secrets > Client secrets, copy the VALUE, not the Secret ID. Permission: none itself. Not needed with a certificate. | secret | awa.models, connectors outlook, sharepoint, teams, microsoft_graph, awa check, awa people |
| `AZURE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH` | Recommended instead of a secret: a PEM file with the private key and the certificate, or a .pfx/.p12 file, whose public part is uploaded under Certificates & secrets > Certificates; it wins over AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET. Permission: none itself. Needs pip install "awa-agents[m365]". | text | connectors outlook, sharepoint, teams, microsoft_graph, awa check, awa people |
| `AZURE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | The password of that key file, if it has one. Permission: none. | secret | connectors outlook, sharepoint, teams, microsoft_graph, awa check, awa people |
| `AZURE_AUTHORITY_HOST` | Entra sign-in host, only for sovereign clouds or a local test server (default `https://login.microsoftonline.com`). Permission: none (*confirm*). | text | awa.models, connectors outlook, sharepoint, teams, microsoft_graph, awa check, awa people |
| `MS_GRAPH_URL` | Microsoft Graph host, only for sovereign clouds or a local test server (default `https://graph.microsoft.com`). Permission: none (*confirm*). | text | connectors outlook, sharepoint, teams, microsoft_graph, awa check, awa people |
| `MS_MAILBOX` | Outlook: the ONE mailbox the process works in (a shared mailbox works too). Permission: application Mail.ReadWrite (plus Mail.Send only to send), limited to this mailbox with Exchange RBAC for Applications; then remove the tenant-wide Mail.* consent. | text | connectors outlook, sharepoint, teams, microsoft_graph, awa check, awa people |
| `MS_SITE_URL` | SharePoint and Excel: the ONE site, such as `https://company.sharepoint.com/sites/sales`. Permission: application Sites.Selected, then an administrator grants 'read' or 'write' on this site. | text | connectors outlook, sharepoint, teams, microsoft_graph, awa check, awa people |
| `MS_CHECK_WORKBOOK` | awa check: the workbook (path in the site's library) the Excel check reads (default: the first .xlsx at the top). Permission: as MS_SITE_URL. | text | awa check |
| `TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL` | Teams: a Workflows webhook (Teams > channel menu > Workflows > 'Send webhook alerts to a channel'; the whole link with sig=). Permission: none in Entra; the link itself is the secret. | secret | connectors outlook, sharepoint, teams, microsoft_graph, awa check, awa people |
| `TEAMS_TEAM_ID` | Teams as a signed-in user (`awa connect microsoft --teams`): the ONE team the agents may use (the groupId= part of the team's link). Permission: delegated ChannelMessage.Send, ChannelMessage.Read.All and User.Read; the user is a member. | text | connectors outlook, sharepoint, teams, microsoft_graph, awa check, awa people |
| `TEAMS_CHANNEL_ID` | The ONE channel of that team (19:...@thread.tacv2, from the channel's link). Permission: as TEAMS_TEAM_ID. | text | connectors outlook, sharepoint, teams, microsoft_graph, awa check, awa people |
| `AWA_CHECK_NEGATIVE_MAILBOX` | awa check: a mailbox the app must NOT be able to read; the check expects 403 (empty skips the negative test). Permission: none. | text | awa check |
| `AWA_CHECK_ALLOW_POST` | awa check: `teams` lets it post ONE test card; empty: it never posts. Permission: as TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL or the Teams user. | `teams` | awa check |

## Storage and runs

| Variable | What it does | Values (default) | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AWA_POSTGRES_DSN` | PostgreSQL database of runs, queues, checkpoints and stores (postgresql://user:password@host:5432/db). Unset: files next to the blueprint. | secret | awa serve, awa worker, awa runs, awa.persistence |
| `AWA_POSTGRES_ADMIN_DSN` | Direct PostgreSQL connection (not through PgBouncer) for setup locks. Unset: AWA_POSTGRES_DSN. | secret | awa serve, awa worker, awa store |
| `AWA_POSTGRES_POOL_MAX` | Connections of the one PostgreSQL pool each process shares. | a number (`10`) | awa serve, awa worker |
| `AWA_POSTGRES_POOLER` | `pgbouncer` when connections go through PgBouncer's transaction pooling (then no prepared statements). | `none`, `pgbouncer` (`none`) | awa serve, awa worker |
| `AWA_DATA_BACKEND` | Where runs, steps and results are kept: `sqlite` (.awa/awa.db) or `postgres`. Unset: `postgres` when AWA_POSTGRES_DSN is set. `awa store use` changes it. | `sqlite`, `postgres` | awa serve, awa worker, awa runs, awa store |
| `AWA_CAPTURE_CONTENT` | Keep prompts, answers and tool bodies of process runs (read only by the auditor role). Off: only their length. | `true`, `false` (`false`) | awa serve, awa worker |
| `AWA_RUN_RETENTION_DAYS` | Days a finished process run is kept before `awa store sweep` deletes it. Unset: kept until deleted. | a number | awa store sweep |
| `AWA_PSEUDONYM_KEY` | Secret that links people to their runs as an HMAC, for erasure per person (written into .env on first local use). | secret | awa serve, awa worker, awa store erase |
| `AWA_PSEUDONYM_KEY_ID` | Version of AWA_PSEUDONYM_KEY, kept with each link. | text (`1`) | awa serve, awa worker |
| `AWA_CHECKPOINTER_BACKEND` | Checkpointer of `awa.persistence.open_checkpointer` (library use; the CLI chooses its own). | `memory`, `sqlite`, `postgres` (`memory`) | awa.persistence (library) |
| `AWA_CHECKPOINTER_PATH` | File of the `sqlite` checkpointer (default .awa/checkpoints.db). | text | awa.persistence (library) |
| `AWA_ARTIFACT_BACKEND` | Artifact repository of `awa.persistence.open_artifact_repository`. | `memory`, `file`, `postgres` (`memory`) | awa.persistence (library) |
| `AWA_ARTIFACT_DIR` | Folder of the `file` artifact backend (default .awa_artifacts). | text | awa.persistence (library) |
| `AWA_STORE_BACKEND` | Store of `awa.persistence.open_store`. | `memory`, `postgres` (`memory`) | awa.persistence (library) |

| `AWA_LANGFUSE_CAPTURE_CONTENT` | Also send prompts, replies and tool data, redacted (off: names, ids, tokens, cost, timing). | `true`, `false` (`false`) | Langfuse tracing |

| `LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT` | Langfuse environment of every trace (`development`, `production`, ...). | text | Langfuse tracing |

## Caching

| Variable | What it does | Values (default) | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AWA_CACHE_ENABLED` | Master switch of every awa cache; the AWA_CACHE_* values win over a blueprint's `defaults.cache`. | `true`, `false` | awa.runtime.cache |
| `AWA_CACHE_PROMPT` | Provider prompt caching: `auto`, `off` or `1h`. | `auto`, `off`, `1h` | awa.runtime.cache |
| `AWA_CACHE_PROMPT_PAD` | Lengthen an OpenAI/Azure prompt prefix that is just short of the 1,024-token caching minimum, so repeated calls read it from the cache (default on). | `true`, `false` | awa.runtime.cache |
| `AWA_CACHE_TOOLS` | Reuse the results of read-only tools. | `true`, `false` | awa.runtime.cache |
| `AWA_CACHE_TOOLS_TTL` | Seconds a read-only tool result is kept across runs (unset: for one run). | a number | awa.runtime.cache |
| `AWA_CACHE_STEPS` | Reuse deterministic process steps. | `true`, `false` | awa.runtime.cache |
| `AWA_CACHE_STORE` | Where the caches are kept: `memory` or `sqlite`. | `memory`, `sqlite` | awa.runtime.cache |
| `AWA_CACHE_PATH` | File of the `sqlite` cache store (default .awa/cache.db). | text | awa.runtime.cache |
| `AWA_CACHE_SALT` | Project secret that makes the cache keys sent to a provider opaque and stable (`awa cache salt` writes one). | secret | awa.runtime.cache, awa cache salt |

## Run limits and loop protection

| Variable | What it does | Values (default) | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AWA_RUN_MAX_REQUESTS` | Model calls one run tree may make when its `UsageLimits` set no `max_requests` (a whole number; a ceiling cannot be switched off, only raised). | a number (`400`) | awa.runtime.termination |
| `AWA_RUN_MAX_TOOL_CALLS` | Tool calls one run tree may make when its `UsageLimits` set no `max_tool_calls`. | a number (`200`) | awa.runtime.termination |
| `AWA_RUN_MAX_TOKENS` | Input plus output tokens one run tree may use when its `UsageLimits` set no `max_total_tokens`. | a number (`1000000`) | awa.runtime.termination |
| `AWA_RUN_MAX_SECONDS` | Wall-clock seconds of a run tree that has no `timeout` and no `UsageLimits.max_duration`. | a number (`3600`) | awa.runtime.termination |
| `AWA_RUN_MAX_DEPTH` | How deep runs may nest (agents delegating to or calling agents); the top-level run has depth 0. | a number (`16`) | awa.runtime.termination |
| `AWA_DELEGATION_MAX_REQUESTS` | Model calls one team delegation may make, its own delegations included, when `TeamLimits.delegation_limits` is not set; beyond it only that delegation stops. | a number (`50`) | awa.team |
| `AWA_MAX_IDENTICAL_CALLS` | Identical tool calls (same tool, arguments and result) in one agent run before the run is stopped for making no progress (at least 2). | a number (`5`) | awa.runtime.termination |
| `AWA_MAX_TOOL_ERRORS` | Failures in a row of one tool in one agent run before the run is stopped for making no progress. | a number (`5`) | awa.runtime.termination |
| `AWA_MAX_IDENTICAL_OUTPUTS` | Identical results in a row after which a `Loop` stops, and identical drafts after which a `Checked` revision stops (at least 2). | a number (`2`) | awa.workflows |
| `AWA_MAX_PAGES_PER_CALL` | Pages one connector list call reads before it returns a `next_page` to continue. | a number (`20`) | awa.connectors |
| `AWA_TOOL_PROFILE` | Defaults of the tool layer: `cost` (results above 6,000 characters saved aside with a preview, clearing from 10,000 tokens) or `quality` (results cut at 40,000 characters, clearing from 40,000 tokens). | `cost`, `quality` (`cost`) | awa.tools.offload, awa.memory.context_editing |
| `AWA_TOOL_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS` | Longest text result a tool hands to the model; unset: the profile's value. In the `cost` profile a longer result is saved aside and the model gets a preview and a reference it can read on with `read_tool_result`. | a number | awa.tools.offload |
| `AWA_TOOL_CIRCUIT_BREAKER` | Failures in a row after which a tool answers 'unavailable in this run' without being called (0: never). | a number (`3`) | awa.tools.resilience |
| `AWA_TOOL_RETRIES` | Retries, with jittered backoff, of a call of a tool that does not act outside the agent and raised a network error. | a number (`2`) | awa.tools.resilience |
| `AWA_CONTEXT_EDITING` | Replace older tool results with a short note naming the call in what the model sees once a request grows past `AWA_CONTEXT_EDITING_TRIGGER` (the run's state keeps them). | `true`, `false` (`true`) | awa.memory.context_editing |
| `AWA_CONTEXT_EDITING_TRIGGER` | Approximate request size in tokens above which older tool results are cleared; unset: the profile's value (10,000 or 40,000). | a number | awa.memory.context_editing |
| `AWA_CONTEXT_EDITING_KEEP` | Most recent tool results that are never cleared (up to keep + step - 1 stay); unset: the profile's value (3 or 4). | a number | awa.memory.context_editing |
| `AWA_CONTEXT_EDITING_STEP` | Tool results cleared together, so the cached prompt prefix changes only every few calls. | a number (`4`) | awa.memory.context_editing |
| `AWA_CONTEXT_EDITING_CLEAR_AT_LEAST` | Fewest tokens a clearing step must free, else nothing is cleared (a clearing costs one prompt-cache miss); unset: the profile's value (3,000 or 0). | a number | awa.memory.context_editing |
| `AWA_MAX_LEASE_LOSSES` | Lost worker leases in a row (a worker crashed or hung on the run) after which an automation run is dead-lettered instead of taken over again. | a number (`3`) | awa.automation |

## Local services (awa setup)

| Variable | What it does | Values (default) | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AWA_SETUP_DB_PORT` | Port of the local PostgreSQL on 127.0.0.1. | a number | awa setup services |
| `AWA_SETUP_DB_PASSWORD` | Password of the local PostgreSQL (generated). | secret | awa setup services |
| `AWA_SETUP_LANGFUSE_PORT` | Port of the local Langfuse web UI on 127.0.0.1. | a number | awa setup services |
| `AWA_SETUP_LANGFUSE_ADMIN_EMAIL` | Sign-in email of the local Langfuse. | text | awa setup services |
| `AWA_SETUP_LANGFUSE_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | Sign-in password of the local Langfuse. | secret | awa setup services |
| `AWA_SETUP_LANGFUSE_NEXTAUTH_SECRET` | Session secret of the local Langfuse. | secret | awa setup services |
| `AWA_SETUP_LANGFUSE_SALT` | Salt of the local Langfuse. | secret | awa setup services |
| `AWA_SETUP_LANGFUSE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | Encryption key of the local Langfuse. | secret | awa setup services |
| `AWA_SETUP_LANGFUSE_DB_PASSWORD` | Password of the local Langfuse's PostgreSQL. | secret | awa setup services |
| `AWA_SETUP_LANGFUSE_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` | Password of its ClickHouse. | secret | awa setup services |
| `AWA_SETUP_LANGFUSE_REDIS_PASSWORD` | Password of its Redis. | secret | awa setup services |
| `AWA_SETUP_LANGFUSE_MINIO_PASSWORD` | Password of its MinIO object store. | secret | awa setup services |

## General

| Variable | What it does | Values (default) | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AWA_PROJECT_DIR` | The project folder (default: found from the current folder, see --project). | text | awa CLI |
| `AWA_STRICT_SETTINGS` | Stop with exit code 78 on an unknown AWA_* name or an unconfirmed security switch. | `true`, `false` (`false`) | awa CLI |

## Names your project declares

A blueprint names further variables in its `*_env` keys: a webhook trigger's
`secret_env`, a mailbox's `username_env` and `password_env`, `api_key_env`, and the
variables of your connectors. awa treats them as secret, reads them from the project
`.env` like the settings above, and `awa doctor` lists them.

<!-- source: reference/tools.md -->

# Tools

Every built-in tool, its approval default and an example call.

A blueprint names a built-in tool as `builtin:<tool>`; in Python, `awa.toolkits.catalog()` creates
it (see [Built-in toolkits](../develop/tools.md#builtin-toolkits)). Tools that change the outside world (write, delete,
send, post, run a changing statement) wait for a person's approval by default.

<!-- generated by scripts/gen_tool_matrix.py: tool table -->

| Tool | Category | Risk | Approval default | Side effect | Example | Contract cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fetch_url` | web | untrusted input, external action | no | none | [`tool_fetch_url.py`](#fetch_url) | valid, invalid, 4 hostile, injection framed, side effect |
| `web_search` | web | untrusted input | no | none | [`tool_web_search.py`](#web_search) | valid, invalid, 1 hostile, injection framed, side effect |
| `verify_quote` | web | untrusted input, external action | no | none | [`tool_verify_quote.py`](#verify_quote) | valid, invalid, 2 hostile, injection not repeated, side effect |
| `list_files` | files | private data | no | none | [`tool_list_files.py`](#list_files) | valid, invalid, 3 hostile, side effect |
| `read_file` | files | untrusted input, private data | no | none | [`tool_read_file.py`](#read_file) | valid, invalid, 4 hostile, injection framed, side effect |
| `write_file` | files | external action | yes | same state when repeated | [`tool_write_file.py`](#write_file) | valid, invalid, 3 hostile, side effect, approval gate |
| `append_file` | files | external action | yes | acts again when repeated | [`tool_append_file.py`](#append_file) | valid, invalid, 2 hostile, side effect, approval gate |
| `move_file` | files | external action | yes | same state when repeated | [`tool_move_file.py`](#move_file) | valid, invalid, 2 hostile, side effect, approval gate |
| `delete_file` | files | external action | yes | same state when repeated | [`tool_delete_file.py`](#delete_file) | valid, invalid, 3 hostile, side effect, approval gate |
| `read_csv` | data | untrusted input, private data | no | none | [`tool_read_csv.py`](#read_csv) | valid, invalid, 3 hostile, injection framed, side effect |

| `write_csv` | data | external action | yes | same state when repeated | [`tool_write_csv.py`](#write_csv) | valid, invalid, 2 hostile, side effect, approval gate |

| `sql_execute` | data | private data, external action | yes | acts again when repeated | [`tool_sql_execute.py`](#sql_execute) | valid, invalid, 3 hostile, side effect, approval gate |

| `extract_pdfs_text` | documents | untrusted input, private data | no | none | [`tool_extract_pdfs_text.py`](#extract_pdfs_text) | valid, invalid, 5 hostile, injection framed, side effect |
